                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch10-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                              All of the following were in the Treaty of Paris of 1783 EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                              1. A The west beyond the Appalachians went to the Americans
                                                                                                                                              2. B Britain recognized American independence
                                                                                                                                              3. C Quebec and its surroundings were ceded to the Americans
                                                                                                                                              4. D Loyalists could seek return of seized property
                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                              The 1783 treaty recognized independence and granted the trans-Appalachian west, but Canada remained British and Loyalists were promised a chance to recover confiscated property.

                                                                                                                                              • A: This was in the treaty: Britain ceded the trans-Appalachian west, with the Mississippi as the new nation's western boundary.
                                                                                                                                              • B: This was in the treaty: Britain formally recognized the independence of the United States.
                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct — this is the exception. Quebec and Canada were not ceded; they remained British, and the new United States–Canadian boundary ran along the Great Lakes.
                                                                                                                                              • D: This was in the treaty: Article V provided that Loyalists could seek the return of confiscated property through the state courts.

                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch10-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                              The fear Washington expresses in the letter most directly shaped which feature of the new Constitution?

                                                                                                                                              1. A A bill of rights guaranteeing the right of rebellion
                                                                                                                                              2. B The prohibition of any national standing army
                                                                                                                                              3. C A federal government strong enough to tax, raise armies, and suppress insurrections
                                                                                                                                              4. D The requirement of unanimous state consent for federal action
                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                              The specter of Shays haunted Philadelphia: the Constitution gave Congress power to tax, raise armies, and call forth the militia 'to execute the Laws of the Union, suppress Insurrections and repel Invasions.' Washington wanted energy in government, not a bill of rights for rebellion, disarmament, or the Articles' unanimity rule.

                                                                                                                                              • A: The Constitution contains no bill of rights guaranteeing rebellion, and Washington was alarmed by the rebellion, not sympathetic to a right of revolt. The Bill of Rights came later, in 1791.
                                                                                                                                              • B: Washington wanted the opposite of banning a standing army. The Constitution authorized Congress to raise and support armies — the very power the Articles had lacked.
                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. The specter of Shays haunted Philadelphia: the Constitution gave the federal government power to tax, raise armies, and call forth the militia to 'suppress Insurrections' — a government with energy enough to enforce its laws.
                                                                                                                                              • D: Unanimous state consent was the Articles' rule — the very paralysis the framers were escaping. The Constitution replaced it with ratification by nine states and majority rule in Congress.

                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch11-mcq-06

                                                                                                                                                  According to the resolves, the Constitution is best described as

                                                                                                                                                  1. A A grant of unlimited power to the federal government
                                                                                                                                                  2. B A compact among sovereign states delegating only certain definite powers
                                                                                                                                                  3. C A treaty between the United States and foreign nations
                                                                                                                                                  4. D A document that abolished the state governments
                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                  Key: B

                                                                                                                                                  The resolves open with compact theory: the states 'constituted a general government for special purposes,' delegating 'certain definite powers' and reserving the rest. The Constitution, in this telling, is a bargain among sovereign states -- not a grant of unlimited federal power, a foreign treaty, or an abolition of the states.

                                                                                                                                                  • A: The Resolutions say the opposite: the states 'are not united on the principle of unlimited submission to their general government.' Unlimited federal power is exactly what the compact theory denies.
                                                                                                                                                  • B: Correct. The Resolutions open with compact theory: the states formed a general government 'for special purposes,' delegating only 'certain definite powers' and reserving the rest — a bargain among sovereign states, not a grant of unlimited power.
                                                                                                                                                  • C: The Constitution is not a treaty with foreign nations. It is the framework of the American government itself — the Resolutions treat it as an agreement among the states.
                                                                                                                                                  • D: The Resolutions did not abolish the state governments; they presuppose them. The whole point of the compact theory is that the states remain sovereign parties to the bargain.

                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch11-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                  Which later development most clearly showed the practical limits of the Kentucky Resolutions' compact theory?

                                                                                                                                                  1. A The Louisiana Purchase
                                                                                                                                                  2. B The War of 1812
                                                                                                                                                  3. C The building of the Erie Canal
                                                                                                                                                  4. D Jackson's threat of military force against nullification
                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                  Key: D

                                                                                                                                                  South Carolina tried to act on the 1798 logic in 1832, but Jackson's proclamation against nullification -- 'disunion by armed force is treason' -- backed by the Force Bill, showed the compact theory could not prevail against a determined president. The compromise tariff defused the crisis, but the theory's practical limit had been demonstrated.

                                                                                                                                                  • A: The Louisiana Purchase (1803) was a triumph of federal power, not a test of compact theory — no state tried to nullify it.
                                                                                                                                                  • B: The War of 1812 tested American arms and unity, but it did not put the Kentucky Resolutions' compact theory into practice.
                                                                                                                                                  • C: The Erie Canal (1825) was a state-built internal improvement. It raised questions about federal versus state projects, but no state invoked compact theory to defy federal law over it.
                                                                                                                                                  • D: Correct. South Carolina tried to act on the 1798 logic in 1832, but Jackson's proclamation against nullification — backed by the Force Bill's threat of military action — showed that a state could not defy federal law in practice. The compromise tariff defused the crisis, but compact theory's practical limit had been demonstrated.

                                                                                                                                                      All of the following help explain why America entered the War of 1812 EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                      1. A The impressment of American sailors
                                                                                                                                                      2. B A powerful American navy eager to prove itself
                                                                                                                                                      3. C British support for western Native tribes
                                                                                                                                                      4. D American designs on Canada and Florida
                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                      Key: B

                                                                                                                                                      America went to war over impressment, British aid to western tribes, and War Hawk hunger for Canada and Florida — but with an army of 6,000 men and 17 ships, no one claimed the navy was ready to show its strength.

                                                                                                                                                      • A: Impressment of American sailors was a real cause: British warships stopped American vessels and seized sailors, an insult the War Hawks would not tolerate.
                                                                                                                                                      • B: Correct — this is the exception. America had no powerful navy eager to prove itself: the regular army numbered about 6,000 men and the navy had roughly 17 ships, so naval ambition did not drive the war.
                                                                                                                                                      • C: British support for western Native tribes was a real cause: Westerners blamed Britain for arming Tecumseh's confederacy and other resisting tribes.
                                                                                                                                                      • D: American designs on Canada and Florida were a real cause: War Hawks like Clay and Calhoun openly coveted Canada and Spanish Florida.

                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch12-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                      Tecumseh's confederacy sought an alliance with Britain during the War of 1812 primarily because

                                                                                                                                                      1. A Tecumseh hoped to make his people British subjects
                                                                                                                                                      2. B Only Britain could supply the arms and diplomatic backing needed to resist the United States
                                                                                                                                                      3. C France had refused to provide any assistance
                                                                                                                                                      4. D Harrison had advised him to seek British aid
                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                      Key: B

                                                                                                                                                      Tecumseh's confederacy needed what only Britain could provide: muskets, powder, and a great-power counterweight to the United States. The alliance was strategic, not cultural -- at the Thames in 1813 Tecumseh died fighting alongside the British, and with him the confederacy died too.

                                                                                                                                                      • A: Tecumseh did not want his people to become British subjects. The alliance was strategic — arms and backing for resistance — not a bid for subjecthood.
                                                                                                                                                      • B: Correct. Tecumseh's confederacy needed what only Britain could provide: muskets, powder, and a great-power counterweight to the United States. At the Thames in 1813 he died fighting alongside the British, and the confederacy died with him.
                                                                                                                                                      • C: France was not a factor: it had sold Louisiana in 1803 and was consumed by the Napoleonic wars. There was no French assistance to refuse.
                                                                                                                                                      • D: Harrison was Tecumseh's enemy, not his adviser. He would never have advised Tecumseh to seek British aid; he was the one Tecumseh was resisting.

                                                                                                                                                      SAQ5s24-ch12-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                      A. Briefly explain ONE example of how foreign wars influenced American policy in the period 1801–1815. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that influence in the same period. C. Briefly explain ONE consequence of the War of 1812.

                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                        A. Napoleon's failure to crush the Haitian slave rebellion, combined with looming war against Britain, convinced him to sell Louisiana in 1803 — doubling the United States at a stroke. B. Jefferson's 1807 Embargo Act, a response to British and French seizures of American ships during the Napoleonic Wars, devastated American commerce and showed how European wars dictated American policy. C. The War of 1812 fostered American nationalism and economic independence: the war spurred domestic manufacturing, discredited the Federalists after Hartford, and ushered in the 'Era of Good Feelings.'

                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch13-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                          President Monroe claimed westward removal would benefit Native Americans because

                                                                                                                                                          1. A They would escape constant harassment west of the Mississippi
                                                                                                                                                          2. B The army would protect them on the journey west
                                                                                                                                                          3. C They would be fairly paid for the lands they left
                                                                                                                                                          4. D Western settlers welcomed Native neighbors
                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                          Key: A

                                                                                                                                                          Monroe argued that east of the Mississippi, Native peoples would face endless harassment from settlers, so removal west — however coercive in practice — was presented as being in their interest.

                                                                                                                                                          • A: Correct. Monroe argued that east of the Mississippi, Native peoples would face constant harassment from settlers, so moving west — however coercive in practice — was presented as being in their own interest.
                                                                                                                                                          • B: The army did not protect Native peoples on the journey west. Removal was enforced by soldiers and proved deadly — the Trail of Tears killed thousands — not a guarded, safe migration.
                                                                                                                                                          • C: Native peoples were not fairly paid for the lands they left. Treaties were signed under duress and compensation was a fraction of the land's value — unfair payment was not Monroe's stated benefit.
                                                                                                                                                          • D: Western settlers did not welcome Native neighbors. Settler pressure for Native land was the very reason removal was proposed, so 'welcoming neighbors' reverses the history.

                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch13-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                          Nullification became a national issue when

                                                                                                                                                          1. A Georgia defied Congress over slavery
                                                                                                                                                          2. B South Carolina nullified Indian-removal laws
                                                                                                                                                          3. C South Carolina nullified the federal tariff bills
                                                                                                                                                          4. D Southern electors bolted in the 1824 election
                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                          Key: C

                                                                                                                                                          South Carolina, enraged by the protective tariffs of 1828 and 1832, declared them null within the state — the Nullification Crisis that Jackson answered with the Force Bill.

                                                                                                                                                          • A: Georgia did defy federal authority, but over Cherokee removal — ignoring the Supreme Court in Worcester v. Georgia — not over slavery, and that was not what made nullification a national crisis.
                                                                                                                                                          • B: South Carolina did not nullify Indian-removal laws. Indian removal was a federal policy the South generally supported; the nullified laws were the protective tariffs.
                                                                                                                                                          • C: Correct. South Carolina, enraged by the protective tariffs of 1828 and 1832, declared them null and void within the state — the Nullification Crisis that Jackson answered with the Force Bill.
                                                                                                                                                          • D: Southern electors did not bolt in the 1824 election over nullification. The 'corrupt bargain' election of 1824 was a different controversy, about the House choosing Adams over Jackson.

                                                                                                                                                          2. B Temperance
                                                                                                                                                          3. C Prison reform
                                                                                                                                                          4. D Public-school reform
                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                          As Massachusetts secretary of education, Mann crusaded for free public schools, better teacher training, and longer school terms — the father of the common-school movement.

                                                                                                                                                          • A: Mann was not an abolitionist leader; that cause belonged to figures like William Lloyd Garrison and Frederick Douglass.

                                                                                                                                                          • C: Mann was not a prison reformer; Dorothea Dix led the campaign for asylums and better treatment of the mentally ill.
                                                                                                                                                          • D: Correct. As Massachusetts secretary of education, Horace Mann crusaded for free public schools, better teacher training, and longer school terms — the father of the common-school movement.

                                                                                                                                                          SAQ5s24-ch13-saq-01

Briefly explain ONE way Andrew Jackson fostered the growth of 'Jacksonian democracy.' B. Briefly explain a SECOND way he fostered it. C. Briefly explain ONE policy promoted by Jackson's political opponents.

                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                            A. Jackson championed the expansion of white male suffrage: property qualifications for voting fell across the states, and the 'common man' entered politics as never before. B. Jackson's victory in the disputed election of 1828 — after the 'corrupt bargain' of 1824 — was hailed as the triumph of the people's will over entrenched elites. C. Jackson's opponents, the National Republicans and later Whigs, promoted Clay's American System: a national bank, protective tariffs, and federally funded internal improvements.

                                                                                                                                                              SAQ5s24-ch14-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                              A. Briefly explain ONE issue that deepened sectional hostility between North and South in the period 1835–1860. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such issue. C. Briefly explain ONE effort to compromise between the sections in this period.

                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                A. Northern abolitionism — pamphlets, petitions, and orators like William Lloyd Garrison — convinced many Southerners that the North meant to destroy their way of life. B. The fight over slavery in the territories acquired from Mexico, from the Wilmot Proviso through 'Bleeding Kansas,' turned westward expansion into a sectional battleground. C. Leaders repeatedly tried compromise: the Missouri Compromise (1820) drew a line at 36°30′, and the Compromise of 1850 patched the Union together for another decade.

                                                                                                                                                                  SAQ5s24-ch15-saq-01

Briefly explain ONE reason the Civil War lasted longer than people initially expected. B. Briefly explain a SECOND reason it lasted so long. C. Briefly explain ONE important turning point of the war.

                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                    A. The Confederacy's vast territory meant the Union had to conquer and occupy an area the size of Western Europe while maintaining a 3,500-mile blockade — a task that took four years. C.                                                                                                                                                                           SAQ5s24-ch17-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                          A. Briefly explain ONE way American settlement rapidly transformed the West in the 25 years after the Civil War. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such transformation. C. Briefly explain ONE way Native Americans resisted American settlement in this period.

                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                            A. The transcontinental railroad, completed at Promontory Summit in 1869, let settlers, cattle, and wheat move cheaply across the continent, knitting the West to eastern markets. B. The Homestead Act (1862) offered 160 acres of public land to settlers, drawing hundreds of thousands of farms onto the Plains. C. Native peoples resisted fiercely: the Sioux destroyed Custer's command at Little Bighorn (1876), and the Ghost Dance movement sought spiritual renewal against white expansion before it was crushed at Wounded Knee (1890).

                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch18-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                              Frederick W. Taylor's methods, embraced by many factory owners,

                                                                                                                                                                              1. A Helped immigrant workers assimilate
                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Guaranteed higher wages and better conditions
                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Sought maximum efficiency in factory operations
                                                                                                                                                                              4. D Required extensive worker training
                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                              Taylor's 'scientific management' broke jobs into timed motions to squeeze maximum output from workers — the intellectual seed of the assembly line.

                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Taylor's system was about squeezing output from workers, not about helping immigrants assimilate. 'Scientific management' treated workers as machines to be timed and optimized, not as newcomers to be welcomed.
                                                                                                                                                                              • B: The opposite of how Taylorism worked in practice. Taylor's methods were meant to raise output — often by cutting wages per unit and speeding up work — not to guarantee workers higher pay or better conditions.
                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. Frederick W. Taylor's 'scientific management' broke factory jobs into timed, standardized motions to wring maximum efficiency and output from every worker — the intellectual seed of the assembly line.
                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Taylor's system deskilled work on purpose: by breaking jobs into tiny, timed motions, it required less skill and less training from workers, not more.

                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch18-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                              All of the following describe the late-nineteenth-century industrial city EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                              1. A Workers lived near factories close to downtown
                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Factories were sited near water for power
                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Downtowns held offices, banks, and insurers
                                                                                                                                                                              4. D Saloons dotted working-class neighborhoods
                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                              Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                              Industrial cities did cluster workers near factories around a downtown of offices and banks, with saloons in working-class wards — but by 1890 steam, not water, powered most industry.

                                                                                                                                                                              • A: True of the era: industrial workers really did live near factories close to downtown, since they walked to work. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Correct — this is the exception. By 1890 steam engines, not waterpower, drove most industry, so factories no longer had to sit beside rivers for power. Water-powered mill towns belonged to an earlier industrial era.
                                                                                                                                                                              • C: True of the era: downtowns really did hold offices, banks, and insurers while workers lived in wards around them. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                              • D: True of the era: saloons really did dot working-class neighborhoods, serving as social centers for immigrant workers. This is not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch18-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                                              The concentration of power Tarbell describes helped produce which of the following?

                                                                                                                                                                              1. A The repeal of all federal business regulation
                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Rockefeller's election to the presidency
                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Progressive Era antitrust action culminating in the 1911 breakup of Standard Oil
                                                                                                                                                                              4. D The nationalization of the American oil industry
                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                              Tarbell's History ran in McClure's (1902-1904) and became ammunition for the Progressive assault on the trusts. In 1911 the Supreme Court, applying the Sherman Antitrust Act, dissolved Standard Oil into 34 separate companies -- the direct legislative and judicial answer to the concentration she documented.

                                                                                                                                                                              • A: The opposite of what happened. Tarbell's expose fueled demands for more federal business regulation, not less — her work helped bring on the Progressive Era's antitrust and regulatory push.
                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Rockefeller never ran for president. The political result of Tarbell's work was not his election but the legal attack on his company.
                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. Tarbell's History of the Standard Oil Company (1902–1904) became ammunition for the Progressive assault on the trusts; in 1911 the Supreme Court, applying the Sherman Antitrust Act, dissolved Standard Oil into 34 separate companies.
                                                                                                                                                                              • D: The American oil industry was never nationalized. The government's answer was breaking Standard Oil up through antitrust law, not taking it over.

                                                                                                                                                                              SAQ5s24-ch18-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                              A. Briefly explain ONE way American political leaders responded to rapid industrial growth in the late nineteenth century. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such response. C. Briefly explain ONE way American workers responded to rapid industrial growth in the same period.

                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                A. Most Gilded Age leaders did nothing: committed to laissez-faire, presidents from Grant to McKinley treated the trusts as natural and beneficial. B. When leaders did act, it was late and limited — the Interstate Commerce Act (1887) and Sherman Antitrust Act (1890) were passed but barely enforced against the great combinations. C. Workers responded by organizing: the Knights of Labor and the American Federation of Labor built national unions, and strikes like Homestead (1892) and Pullman (1894) shook the nation.

                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch19-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                  The Roosevelt Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine was intended

                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A Keeping European powers out of the Western Hemisphere
                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B 'Assisting' Latin states in economic or political crisis
                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Removing hostile governments in the hemisphere
                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D All of the above
                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                  The 1904 Corollary declared the U.S. an 'international police power' that could intervene in Latin America to keep Europeans out, prop up order, and remove unfriendly regimes — all three purposes at once.

                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Keeping European powers out of the Western Hemisphere was the original Monroe Doctrine (1823) and part of the Corollary, but the Corollary went further — it claimed an American right to intervene directly. This alone understates what the Corollary was intended to do.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: 'Assisting' Latin states in crisis — collecting debts, restoring order — was exactly the policing power Roosevelt claimed in 1904, but it was only one piece of the Corollary's purpose.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Removing hostile governments was indeed part of how the Corollary was applied, but again only one piece. The Corollary claimed all of these purposes at once.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Correct. The 1904 Roosevelt Corollary declared the United States an 'international police power' in the Western Hemisphere — empowered to keep Europeans out, intervene in Latin states' crises to preserve order, and remove unfriendly regimes. All three purposes were claimed together.

                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch19-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                  Many American humanitarians first backed the Spanish-American War because

                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A They were horrified by Spain's reconcentration policy in Cuba
                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B They ignored the yellow press's editorials
                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C They wanted to help Filipino natives
                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D They sought American economic interests in Cuba
                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                  Spain's reconcentration camps in Cuba — herding civilians into disease-ridden camps to starve the insurgency — horrified American humanitarians and fed war fever in 1898.

                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Correct. Spain's 'reconcentration' policy — forcing Cuban civilians into disease-ridden camps to starve the insurgency — was widely reported in the American press, and the suffering it caused turned humanitarians toward war against Spain in 1898.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: The opposite of what happened. The yellow press's lurid editorials about Cuban suffering fed the war fever; humanitarians absorbed that coverage rather than ignoring it.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: American humanitarians in 1898 were focused on Cuba, not the Philippines. The war began over Cuba; the Philippine annexation debate — and the humanitarian outcry over subjugating Filipinos — came after the war.
                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Economic interests in Cuba motivated business-minded expansionists, not humanitarians. The humanitarians' argument was about Cuban suffering under Spain, not about sugar profits.

                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B They admired the spirituality of native peoples

                                                                                                                                                                                  A. Briefly explain ONE example of the United States asserting itself as a world power in the period 1890–1913. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that assertion in the same period. C. Briefly explain ONE example of Americans rejecting America's assertion as a world power.

The United States asserted itself by annexing Hawaii in 1898 after American planters overthrew Queen Liliuokalani, extending American sovereignty into the Pacific. B.                                                                                                                                                                                       MCQ5s24-ch20-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                      Progressive reforms achieved all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A City governments like Cleveland's became more efficient
                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B Factory health and safety improved in places
                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C Conditions for migrant farm workers markedly improved
                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D A national income tax was established
                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                      Progressives cleaned up city government, workplaces, and the tax code — but farm laborers, especially migrants, saw little of this reform energy.

                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Cleveland under Tom Johnson really did become a model of efficient, reform-minded city government — this was a genuine Progressive achievement, so it is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Factory health and safety really did improve in places — through state laws on hours, child labor, and workplace conditions. This was real Progressive progress, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: Correct — this is the exception. Progressive reform energy largely bypassed migrant farm workers, who remained outside the era's labor protections and reform campaigns.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: A national income tax really was established — the Sixteenth Amendment (1913) authorized it. This was a genuine Progressive achievement, not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch20-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                      Theodore Roosevelt ran for president in 1912 because

                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A Taft's administration was uniformly anti-progressive
                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B He wanted to split the GOP and elect a Democrat
                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C He was outraged by the Ballinger-Pinchot affair
                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D Taft moved against U.S. Steel under the Sherman Act
                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                      Roosevelt was furious when Taft's Justice Department moved against U.S. Steel — a trust Roosevelt himself had approved — convincing him Taft had betrayed progressivism and driving the 1912 Bull Moose bolt.

                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Taft was not uniformly anti-progressive — he filed more antitrust suits than Roosevelt and supported some reforms. 'Uniformly anti-progressive' overstates the break, and it was not what drove Roosevelt to run.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Roosevelt did not run to split the GOP and elect a Democrat, though that is what happened (Wilson won). His motive was personal and political fury at Taft, not a scheme to hand the election to the Democrats.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: The Ballinger-Pinchot affair angered Roosevelt, but it was an earlier, secondary grievance. What drove him to run in 1912 was the U.S. Steel suit — a trust he had personally approved — which convinced him Taft had betrayed progressivism.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: Correct. Roosevelt was furious when Taft's Justice Department moved against U.S. Steel under the Sherman Act — a combination Roosevelt himself had blessed in 1907. To Roosevelt this proved Taft had turned against the progressive program, and it drove the 1912 Bull Moose bolt.

                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch20-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                                      Progressives and Socialists agreed that

                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A Capitalism had created vast inequality
                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B The factory system must be fundamentally rebuilt
                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C Labor unions were inherently evil
                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D Revolution was the only remedy
                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                      Both camps agreed industrial capitalism had produced obscene inequality — but Progressives wanted to regulate it while Socialists wanted to replace it.

                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Correct. Both camps agreed that industrial capitalism had produced vast, obscene inequality — they split on the remedy: Progressives wanted to regulate capitalism, Socialists wanted to replace it. The agreement was on the diagnosis.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Progressives did not want to rebuild the factory system fundamentally — they wanted to regulate and reform it (safety laws, antitrust). Only the Socialists wanted a fundamental rebuilding.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: Neither camp thought labor unions were inherently evil — both supported organized labor. Hostility to unions was a business position, not a Progressive or Socialist one.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: Only the Socialists saw revolution as the remedy. Progressives explicitly rejected revolution in favor of reform through law and regulation.

                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                      • minor · answer_tell — only one distractor uses absolute wording
                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch20-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                      Who was LEAST likely to be a Progressive in this era?

                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A A Social Gospel minister
                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B A major U.S. Steel stockholder
                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C A follower of Eugene Debs
                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D A Bull Moose Party member
                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                      Social Gospel ministers, Debs followers, and Bull Moosers all marched under the progressive banner — a U.S. Steel magnate, whose trust the Progressives meant to tame, did not.

                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Social Gospel ministers were very likely Progressives — the Social Gospel taught that Christians must reform society's ills, making ministers natural reformers.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Correct. A major U.S. Steel stockholder was the least likely Progressive — U.S. Steel was exactly the kind of giant trust the Progressives meant to tame, and its owners had every interest in resisting regulation.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: A follower of Eugene Debs was likely a Progressive-adjacent reformer — Debs's Socialists shared the Progressives' diagnosis of inequality, even while differing on the cure.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: A Bull Moose Party member was by definition a Progressive — the 1912 Bull Moose (Progressive) Party was Roosevelt's reform vehicle.

                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch20-mcq-06

                                                                                                                                                                                      The inspection system described in the act relied on

                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A Voluntary self-regulation by the packing companies
                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B Continuous federal presence inside plants plus a government stamp of approval
                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C Inspections conducted by the state governments
                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D An outright ban on industrial meatpacking
                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                      The act plants federal inspectors inside the plants -- 'access at all times, by day or night' -- and gives their judgment the force of a government stamp: 'Inspected and passed.' The mechanism is continuous federal presence plus an official seal, not voluntary codes, state action, or prohibition of the industry.

                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: The opposite of the act's approach. The 1906 law did not trust packing companies to regulate themselves — it imposed mandatory federal inspection precisely because voluntary practices had failed.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Correct. The act plants federal inspectors inside the plants — with 'access at all times, by day or night' — and gives their judgment the force of a government stamp: 'Inspected and passed.' The mechanism is continuous federal presence plus an official seal.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: The inspection system was federal, not state. The act created federal inspectors appointed under the Secretary of Agriculture — a national system, not fifty state ones.
                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: The act did not ban industrial meatpacking — it regulated it. Packing continued; it now operated under federal inspection.

                                                                                                                                                                                      SAQ5s24-ch20-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                      A. Briefly explain ONE example of Progressive action to reform the American economy. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of Progressive economic reform. C. Briefly explain ONE example of Progressive action to reform American politics.

                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                        A. Reform mayors like Cleveland's Tom Johnson municipalized utilities to give citizens cheaper, better service, while governors like Wisconsin's La Follette regulated railroads and pushed direct primaries. B. At the federal level, Roosevelt's trust-busting and the Hepburn Act (1906) strengthened railroad regulation, and the Pure Food and Drug and Meat Inspection Acts protected consumers. C. Politically, Progressives pushed direct democracy: the initiative, referendum, recall, direct election of senators (Seventeenth Amendment), and women's suffrage (Nineteenth Amendment).
