                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch21-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                          All of the following moved America toward war with Germany EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A The Sussex Pledge
                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B Germany's 1917 U-boat campaign
                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The sinking of the Lusitania
                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D The Zimmermann Telegram
                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                          Unrestricted U-boat warfare, the Lusitania sinking, and the Zimmermann Telegram all pushed America toward war — but the 1916 Sussex Pledge was Germany promising restraint, the one step away from war.

                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Correct — this is the exception. The 1916 Sussex Pledge was Germany's promise to limit submarine warfare and warn merchant ships — a step back from war, not toward it. It was the one move that eased tensions rather than inflaming them.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Germany's 1917 return to unrestricted U-boat warfare — sinking ships without warning — was the final provocation that pushed Wilson to ask for war. It moved America toward war, so it is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: The 1915 sinking of the Lusitania, killing 128 Americans, outraged the United States and moved it toward war. It is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: The 1917 Zimmermann Telegram — Germany's offer of an alliance to Mexico against the U.S. — inflamed American opinion and moved the country toward war. It is not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch21-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                          France opposed much of Wilson's Fourteen Points because

                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A They opposed any League of Nations
                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B They resented Germany's exclusion from peacemaking
                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C They disdained Wilson personally
                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D They wanted to punish Germany, not reform the world
                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                          Wilson dreamed of a democratic peace, but Clemenceau's France wanted Germany crippled — reparations, territory, and security — clashing fundamentally with the Fourteen Points.

                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: France did not oppose the League as such — France actually wanted a strong alliance system for security against Germany. French objections were about the peace's terms, not about the League existing.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: France had no wish to include Germany in peacemaking — Clemenceau wanted Germany excluded and punished. Resenting Germany's exclusion would have been Germany's complaint, not France's.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: Clemenceau and Wilson clashed personally, but personal disdain was not the basis of French opposition. France's objection was substantive: it wanted security through a weakened Germany, not through Wilson's ideals.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Correct. Wilson dreamed of a democratic peace that would reform the world, but Clemenceau's France wanted Germany crippled — reparations, lost territory, military limits. France's demand for punishment clashed fundamentally with the Fourteen Points' vision.

                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                          • major · answer_tell — keyed answer is uniquely and substantially longest
                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch21-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                                                                          After America declared war in 1917,

                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A Ration cards went to every family
                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B German-Americans were herded into camps
                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C Cities drilled for enemy attack
                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D Celebrities helped sell Liberty Bonds
                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                          The home front mobilized through Liberty Bond drives — with stars like Chaplin and Fairbanks headlining rallies — plus the draft, war industries, and propaganda. There were no ration cards or German-American camps.

                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: There were no general ration cards for American families in World War I — food conservation was voluntary ('Meatless Mondays,' 'Wheatless Wednesdays'), not rationed. Ration cards came in World War II.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: German-Americans faced intense suspicion and harassment, but they were not herded into camps. Internment camps were a World War II policy against Japanese-Americans, not a World War I policy against German-Americans.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: American cities did not drill for enemy attack in 1917 — the war was an ocean away and German bombers could not reach the U.S. Air-raid drills belong to later wars.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Correct. The home front mobilized through Liberty Bond drives — with celebrities like Charlie Chaplin and Douglas Fairbanks headlining rallies — plus the draft, war industries, and propaganda. There were no ration cards or German-American internment camps.

                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch21-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                                                                          Wilson's campaign for the League of Nations failed in the Senate primarily because

                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A He refused to accept Lodge's reservations to the treaty
                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B The American people opposed any peace treaty at all
                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The League of Nations was never formally proposed
                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D Senate Republicans united behind Wilson's version
                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                          Lodge offered reservations -- especially protecting Congress's war power against Article X -- that a majority of senators could accept. Wilson, shattered by his stroke and rigid in idealism, ordered loyal Democrats to vote against the treaty with reservations attached, defeating his own League rather than compromising.

                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Correct. Lodge offered reservations — especially protecting Congress's war power against Article X — that a Senate majority could accept. Wilson, shattered by his stroke and rigid in his idealism, ordered loyal Democrats to vote against the treaty with the reservations attached, defeating his own League rather than compromising.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: The American people did not oppose any peace treaty — the country wanted peace and many supported the League. The failure was in the Senate, driven by Wilson's refusal to compromise on the reservations.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: The League of Nations was formally proposed — in the Treaty of Versailles, which Wilson signed and brought home. The proposal was real; it was Wilson's all-or-nothing stance that killed it in the Senate.
                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Senate Republicans did not unite behind Wilson's version — Lodge led the opposition precisely to force reservations on the treaty. It was the Democrats, following Wilson's orders, who voted down the treaty with reservations.

                                                                                                                                                                                          A. Briefly explain ONE step the American government took to mobilize the people for World War I. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such mobilization step. C. Briefly explain ONE American military contribution to Allied victory in World War I.

                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                            A. Washington financed the war by selling Liberty Bonds, promoted by celebrities at rallies across the country. B. The Food Administration under Herbert Hoover regulated production and consumption with 'wheatless Mondays' and 'meatless Tuesdays,' while the Lever Act gave the government broad economic controls. C. America's fresh troops and supplies tipped the balance: the 1918 offensives, with two million American soldiers in France, broke the exhausted German lines.

                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch22-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                              The novel that most fully endorsed 1920s business philosophy was

                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A Main Street
                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B The Great Gatsby
                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C The Man Nobody Knows
                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D Babbitt
                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                              Bruce Barton's The Man Nobody Knows (1925) recast Jesus as a master salesman and businessman — the decade's definitive celebration of commerce, unlike Lewis's satires or Fitzgerald's critique.

                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Main Street (1920) satirized small-town life and its boosterism — Sinclair Lewis mocked the business mentality, he did not endorse it.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: The Great Gatsby (1925) critiqued the hollowness of Jazz Age wealth — Fitzgerald exposed the emptiness behind the glitter, not a celebration of business philosophy.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. Bruce Barton's The Man Nobody Knows (1925) recast Jesus as a master salesman and businessman — a direct celebration of commerce and advertising, the decade's definitive endorsement of business philosophy.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Babbitt (1922) satirized the conformist businessman — Lewis held George Babbitt up for ridicule, not admiration.

                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch22-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                              Hoover's 1928 election demonstrated all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A Voters credited Republicans for prosperity
                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Urban-rural divisions had faded
                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Prohibition remained a hot-button issue
                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D America rejected a Catholic candidate
                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                              Hoover's landslide showed faith in Republican prosperity, the salience of Prohibition, and anti-Catholic resistance to Al Smith — but it did not heal the urban-rural divide, which yawned wider than ever.

                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Voters really did credit Republicans for prosperity in 1928 — 'a chicken in every pot' Hoover ran on continued Republican good times. This was demonstrated by the election, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Correct — this is the exception. The urban-rural divide did not fade in 1928 — it yawned wider than ever, with Smith carrying the big cities and Hoover sweeping the countryside. The election exposed the split, it did not heal it.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Prohibition really did remain a hot-button issue in 1928 — Smith was wet, Hoover dry, and the issue divided voters sharply. This was demonstrated, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: America really did reject a Catholic candidate in 1928 — anti-Catholic prejudice hurt Al Smith badly, especially in the South and Midwest. This was demonstrated, not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                              QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                              • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch22-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                                                              Many American writers of the 1920s, disillusioned with American life, responded by

                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A they joined the Communist Party in large numbers
                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B they abandoned literature for electoral politics
                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C they moved to Paris and wrote as expatriates
                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D they emigrated to the Soviet Union
                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                              The 'Lost Generation' -- Hemingway, Fitzgerald, Dos Passos -- fled to Paris, where Gertrude Stein's salon became their headquarters. Exile was itself the critique: they found the prosperous America Parker satirized spiritually empty and went abroad to write about it.

                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: American writers did not join the Communist Party in large numbers in the 1920s. The characteristic response of the disillusioned was exile, not party membership.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: They did not abandon literature for electoral politics — they kept writing. Their response was to write from abroad, not to run for office.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. The 'Lost Generation' — Hemingway, Fitzgerald, Dos Passos — moved to Paris, where Gertrude Stein's salon became their headquarters. Exile was itself the critique: they found prosperous America spiritually empty and went abroad to write about it.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: They did not emigrate to the Soviet Union — their chosen exile was Paris, not Moscow. The Lost Generation's destination was literary Paris.

                                                                                                                                                                                              SAQ5s24-ch22-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                              A. Briefly explain ONE example of social or cultural change in the 1920s. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that change. C. Briefly explain ONE example of resistance to social or cultural change in the 1920s.

                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                A. Mass consumer culture arrived: radios, refrigerators, and automobiles bought on installment plans, sold by a new advertising industry, reshaped daily life. B. Women claimed new freedoms — the flapper, the vote (1920), and public figures from Dorothy Parker to Aimee Semple McPherson embodying female voices in literature and religion. C. Resistance was fierce: Prohibition, the Scopes trial over evolution, the reborn Ku Klux Klan, and the 1924 immigration quotas defended a 'traditional' America against the new culture.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch23-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Wealthy businessmen who opposed FDR's New Deal charged that

                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A It rewarded the undeserving
                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B It smacked of Bolshevism
                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C It overregulated business
                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D All of the above
                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                                  The Liberty League crowd denounced the New Deal on all three grounds: handouts for the undeserving, creeping Bolshevism, and strangling regulation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Opponents really did charge that the New Deal rewarded the undeserving — handouts to people they said should help themselves. This was a real charge, but only one of three.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Opponents really did charge that the New Deal smacked of Bolshevism — the Liberty League called it creeping socialism. This was a real charge, but only one of three.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Opponents really did charge that the New Deal overregulated business — strangling enterprise with federal rules. This was a real charge, but only one of three.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Correct — all three. Wealthy opponents, organized in the American Liberty League, denounced the New Deal on all three grounds: handouts for the undeserving, creeping Bolshevism, and strangling regulation of business.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • major · answer_tell — all/none-of-the-above option is disallowed
                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch23-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                                                                                  The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation was created to

                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A Guarantee retirement income for the poor
                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B Audit the books of major corporations
                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Insure individual bank deposits
                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D Extend government control of the economy
                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                  After the 1933 bank holiday, the FDIC insured individual deposits in sound banks — restoring the confidence bank runs had destroyed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Guaranteeing retirement income was the job of Social Security (1935), not the FDIC. The FDIC dealt with banks, not pensions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Auditing corporate books was the job of the Securities and Exchange Commission (1934), not the FDIC. The FDIC insured deposits; it did not audit corporations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Correct. Created in 1933 after the bank holiday, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insured individual bank deposits in sound banks — restoring the public confidence that bank runs had destroyed.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: The FDIC's purpose was narrower than 'government control of the economy' — it insured deposits to stop bank panics. It did not extend general economic control; that description misreads a confidence-restoring measure as a power grab.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch23-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                                  The popularity of Huey Long and Father Coughlin showed that

                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A The New Deal had gone too far
                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B Americans were turning to religion
                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Americans wanted truly radical solutions
                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D The government should do more to fight the Depression
                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Long's 'Share Our Wealth' and Coughlin's radio populism drew millions precisely because they said Roosevelt wasn't doing enough — pressure from the left, not the right.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Long and Coughlin did not think the New Deal had gone too far — they attacked it from the left, saying it had not gone far enough. Their pressure was for more action, not less.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Coughlin was a priest, but the popularity of the two men was not about Americans turning to religion — it was about economic desperation. Long was a secular populist; their common ground was economic radicalism, not faith.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: They did not call for truly radical solutions like revolution — Long's 'Share Our Wealth' and Coughlin's populism worked within the system. Their appeal showed demand for more government action, not for revolution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Correct. Long's 'Share Our Wealth' and Coughlin's radio populism drew millions precisely because they said Roosevelt wasn't doing enough to fight the Depression — pressure from the left demanding the government do more, not from the right.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • major · answer_tell — keyed answer is uniquely and substantially longest
                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch23-mcq-06

                                                                                                                                                                                                  According to the passage, Townsend argued his pensions would help the economy because

                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A Pensioners would have to spend the money immediately, stimulating production
                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B The government would save money on relief programs
                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Young workers would earn higher wages
                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D Banks would receive the pension funds as deposits
                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Townsend's pitch is in the passage: pension money 'put into circulation would so stimulate the productive ability of America.' The plan required the $200 to be spent within the month -- forced spending as economic stimulus. It promised no government savings, no wage hikes for the young, and no bank deposits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Correct. Townsend's pitch, quoted in the passage, was that pension money 'put into circulation would so stimulate the productive ability of America.' The plan required the $200 to be spent within the month — forced spending as economic stimulus. The passage promises no government savings, no wage hikes for the young, and no bank deposits.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: The passage promises no government savings — Roosevelt in fact calls the plan impractical and harmful. Saving money on relief was never Townsend's argument.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: The passage says nothing about young workers earning higher wages. Townsend's argument was about pensioners spending money, not about raising the young's pay.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: The passage says nothing about banks receiving pension funds as deposits — the money was to be spent immediately, which is the opposite of being saved in banks.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch23-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Roosevelt viewed movements like Townsend's as

                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A as a welcome ally of the New Deal
                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B as a communist front to be suppressed
                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C as a political threat to be outflanked with his own pension plan
                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D as too marginal to deserve his attention
                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                  Roosevelt privately called pension demagogues like Townsend, Coughlin, and Long a political menace and moved to 'steal their thunder' -- his phrase -- by putting old-age insurance into the Social Security Act. The movements were rivals to be outflanked, not allies, and FDR took them very seriously indeed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Roosevelt did not see Townsend as a welcome ally — the passage shows him calling the plan 'obviously impractical' and harmful. The movements were rivals, not partners.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Roosevelt did not treat Townsend as a communist front to be suppressed — Townsend's movement was a populist pension crusade, not a communist one, and FDR's response was political outflanking, not suppression.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Correct. Roosevelt privately treated pension demagogues like Townsend, Coughlin, and Long as a political menace and moved to 'steal their thunder' — his phrase — by putting old-age insurance into the Social Security Act. The movements were rivals to be outflanked, and FDR took them very seriously.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Roosevelt did not consider the movement too marginal to notice — the passage and his political response show he took it as a serious threat worth answering with his own pension plan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                  SAQ5s24-ch23-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                  A. Briefly explain ONE way government expanded to combat the Great Depression. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that expansion. C. Briefly explain ONE example of resistance to the expansion of government in the 1930s.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                    A. Hoover created the Reconstruction Finance Corporation (1932) to lend to banks and businesses, breaking with pure voluntarism. B. Roosevelt's Hundred Days vastly expanded Washington: the AAA, CCC, TVA, and FDIC put the federal government into farming, employment, power, and banking. C. Resistance came from both sides: business leaders denounced the New Deal as socialism (the Liberty League), while the Supreme Court struck down the NRA and AAA in 1935–36.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch24-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Later critics attacked the Yalta Conference for all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A The USSR got control of most of Germany
                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B The Soviets' Japan pledge was vague
                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C Roosevelt was visibly near death
                                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D Soviet-liberated nations stayed under Moscow
                                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                      Germany was divided into four occupation zones, not handed to Moscow; critics' real complaints were Yalta's blessing of Soviet domination in Eastern Europe, the vague promise of Japanese war entry, and Roosevelt's failing health.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Correct — this is the exception. Germany was divided into four occupation zones (American, British, French, Soviet) — the USSR never got control of most of Germany. Critics' real complaints were about Eastern Europe, the vague Japan pledge, and Roosevelt's failing health.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: The Soviets' vague pledge to enter the war against Japan really was a criticism of Yalta — critics attacked the concessions Roosevelt made to secure it. This was a real complaint, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: Roosevelt's visibly failing health really was a criticism — critics argued he was too ill to bargain hard with Stalin. This was a real complaint, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: Soviet-liberated nations staying under Moscow really was a criticism — Yalta's blessing of Soviet domination in Eastern Europe was the critics' central grievance. This was a real complaint, not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                      SAQ5s24-ch24-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                      A. Briefly explain ONE example of an American military contribution to Allied victory in World War II. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that military contribution. C. Briefly explain ONE effect of World War II on the American home front.

                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                        A. American industry became the 'Arsenal of Democracy': Lend-Lease (1941) shipped tanks, trucks, and planes to Britain and the USSR before America even entered the war. B. American forces turned the tide in both theaters — halting Japan at Midway (1942) and opening the second front with the D-Day invasion of Normandy (1944). C. The home front was transformed: women entered factories as 'Rosie the Riveter,' African Americans migrated to war jobs, and the federal government managed the economy through rationing and price controls.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch25-mcq-02

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The policy of containment held that America should

                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A Dislodge Communist regimes wherever they existed
                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B Hold firm against Communist expansion worldwide
                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C Threaten atomic war against the USSR
                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D Rely on Western European allies
                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Kennan's containment meant holding the line against Soviet expansion everywhere — not rolling communism back, not nuking Moscow.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Dislodging Communist regimes wherever they existed was 'rollback,' not containment. Containment accepted existing Communist states and sought to stop their spread, not to overthrow them.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Correct. George Kennan's containment policy held that America should hold firm against Communist expansion worldwide — stopping the spread of Soviet influence without trying to roll back communism where it already ruled.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: Threatening atomic war against the USSR was 'massive retaliation,' a later Eisenhower doctrine — not containment. Containment was about political and economic pressure, not nuclear threats.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Relying on Western European allies was part of how containment was carried out (NATO, the Marshall Plan), but it was not what the policy held. Containment was a global doctrine of holding the line, not a doctrine of dependence on allies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch25-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                                                                          HUAC's investigations most directly continued the precedent of

                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A The Whiskey Rebellion prosecutions of the 1790s
                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B The Palmer Raids of 1919-1920
                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The Dred Scott decision
                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D The Teapot Dome investigation
                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Both were federal anti-radical campaigns driven by fear of revolution: Attorney General Palmer's 1919-1920 raids rounded up and deported thousands of suspected radicals in the First Red Scare, just as HUAC's hearings hunted suspected communists in the Second. The Whiskey prosecutions, Dred Scott, and Teapot Dome belong to entirely different stories.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: The Whiskey Rebellion prosecutions were about tax resistance in the 1790s, not about hunting radicals for their beliefs. They belong to a different story entirely.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Correct. Both were federal anti-radical campaigns driven by fear of revolution: Attorney General Palmer's 1919–1920 raids rounded up and deported thousands of suspected radicals in the First Red Scare, just as HUAC's hearings hunted suspected communists in the Second.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: The Dred Scott decision was about slavery and citizenship in 1857, not about investigating radicals. It belongs to an entirely different story.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: The Teapot Dome investigation was about oil-lease corruption in the 1920s, not about anti-communism. It belongs to an entirely different story.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                          SAQ5s24-ch25-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                          A. Briefly explain ONE American effort to contain communism overseas, 1945–1960. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such overseas effort. C. Briefly explain ONE effort to combat communism within the United States in the same period.

                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                            A. The Truman Doctrine (1947) pledged American aid to any nation resisting communism, first applied to Greece and Turkey. B. The Marshall Plan poured $13 billion into Western Europe's recovery to keep war-ravaged nations from turning Communist, and NATO (1949) bound America to Europe's defense. C. At home, Truman's loyalty program investigated federal employees, HUAC probed Hollywood and government, and McCarthyism purged suspected communists from public life.
