                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch26-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Consumer spending rose in the 1950s because of all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A A renewed rush to buy stocks
                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Surging automobile purchases
                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C A boom in home buying
                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D The power of advertising
                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Postwar consumers bought cars, homes, and appliances on a tidal wave of advertising — but stock speculation was not the engine; most families bought goods, not equities.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Correct — this is the exception. There was no renewed rush to buy stocks in the 1950s — most families bought cars, homes, and appliances, not equities. Stock speculation did not drive the consumer boom.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Surging automobile purchases really did drive 1950s consumer spending — cars were the decade's defining purchase. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: A boom in home buying really did drive spending — suburban homeownership exploded with the GI Bill and Levittowns. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: The power of advertising really did drive spending — television ads created mass consumer desire. This is not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch26-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Many Americans especially feared rock 'n' roll because

                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A Many of its musicians and roots were Black
                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B Its stars came from lower-class backgrounds
                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Its stars came from the South
                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D Its lyrics promoted communism
                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Elvis was Southern and working-class, but what truly alarmed respectable America was that rock 'n' roll's roots — and many of its musicians — were Black.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Correct. What truly alarmed respectable America was that rock 'n' roll's roots — and many of its musicians — were Black: the music grew out of rhythm and blues, and its crossing of the color line frightened a segregated society.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Elvis was working-class, but class was not what especially frightened Americans — working-class stars were common. The racial dimension was the deeper alarm.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Elvis was Southern, but Southern origins alone did not cause the fear — country music was Southern too. What frightened people was the music's Black roots.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Rock lyrics did not promote communism — the songs were about love, cars, and dancing. Communism was never the issue; race and sexuality were.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch26-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Spock's reassuring guidance to parents reflected which broader postwar trend?

                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A The decline of medical and scientific authority
                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B A government takeover of child-rearing
                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C A new expert culture of child psychology shaping family life
                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D A return to Victorian child-rearing manuals
                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                              Spock's Baby and Child Care was the flagship of a new postwar expert culture -- pediatricians, child psychologists, and advice columnists guiding suburban family life. Medical authority did not decline; it expanded into the nursery. The government ran no nurseries, and Victorian manuals were exactly what Spock displaced.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Medical and scientific authority did not decline — it expanded. Spock's book was itself an exercise of expert authority over family life, not a retreat from it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: There was no government takeover of child-rearing — no state nurseries or federal parenting programs. Spock's influence came through books and media, not government.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. Spock's Baby and Child Care was the flagship of a new postwar expert culture — pediatricians, child psychologists, and advice columnists guiding suburban family life. His authority over the nursery was expert authority, newly extended.
                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Victorian child-rearing manuals were exactly what Spock displaced — rigid, moralistic, and strict. His permissive guidance was the break from them, not a return.

                                                                                                                                                                                                              QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                              • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                              SAQ5s24-ch26-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                              A. Briefly explain ONE social phenomenon reflecting American prosperity in the 1950s. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such phenomenon. C. Briefly explain ONE critique of prosperous 1950s American society.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                A. Suburbanization exploded: Levittown-style developments, the GI Bill's cheap mortgages, and the 1956 interstate highway system moved millions to car-centered suburbs. B. Consumer culture boomed — automobiles, televisions, and appliances filled suburban homes, and Galbraith dubbed America 'the affluent society.' C. Critics pushed back: suburban conformity, materialism, and the exclusion of minorities drew fire from writers, sociologists, and the emerging civil rights movement.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch27-mcq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The initial fate of the Freedom Riders demonstrated that

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A Southerners had accepted integration orders
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B State governments enforced civil rights laws
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Television news held a powerful grip on the public
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D Washington was committed to protecting civil rights
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The burning buses and beaten riders of 1961 horrified the nation on TV — but neither Washington nor the states moved decisively to protect civil rights workers at that point.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: The opposite of what happened — Southerners violently resisted integration, burning the Freedom Riders' buses and beating the riders. Acceptance was nowhere in sight in 1961.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: The opposite of what happened — state governments in the South protected the attackers, not the riders. Federal protection came only after the violence made national news.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Correct. The burning buses and beaten riders of 1961 horrified the nation on television — the images had a powerful grip on the public. But neither Washington nor the states moved decisively to protect civil rights workers at that point.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Washington was not yet committed to protecting civil rights workers in 1961 — the Kennedy administration intervened reluctantly and belatedly. Commitment came later, after further violence.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch27-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SDS membership was at its all-time high when

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A The draft sent more young men to Vietnam, 1965–67
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B Southern civil rights struggles aired on TV
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Nixon invaded Cambodia
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D Nixon's 1972 bombing peaked
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SDS peaked during the 1965–67 escalation, when the draft touched millions of students; by Cambodia (1970) and the 1972 bombing, it had splintered into factions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: Correct. SDS peaked during the 1965–67 escalation, when the draft touched millions of students — membership was at its all-time high then. By the Cambodia invasion (1970) and the 1972 bombing, the organization had splintered into factions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Southern civil rights struggles on TV mobilized many students, but they were not what drove SDS to its peak membership. The draft and the Vietnam escalation were the engines of its growth.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Nixon's invasion of Cambodia came in 1970 — after SDS had already splintered. Cambodia triggered protests, but not an SDS membership peak.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Nixon's 1972 bombing came after SDS's collapse — by then the organization had broken apart. It could not have been the moment of peak membership.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch27-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Northern Blacks were drawn to 'Black Power' for all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A King seemed focused on the South, not the ghetto
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B Northern ghettos remained poor and hopeless
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Malcolm X and Carmichael evoked Black pride
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D Vast numbers joined the Nation of Islam
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Northern Blacks embraced Black Power as King's integrationism seemed distant, ghettos stayed poor, and Malcolm X and Carmichael offered pride — but only a small minority actually joined the Nation of Islam.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: King really did seem focused on the South, not the Northern ghetto — a genuine reason Northern Blacks turned to Black Power. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Northern ghettos really did remain poor and hopeless — a genuine reason. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Malcolm X and Stokely Carmichael really did evoke Black pride — a genuine reason. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: Correct — this is the exception. Only a small minority of Black Americans actually joined the Nation of Islam. The turn to Black Power was broad; formal membership in the Nation of Islam was not.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MCQ5s24-ch27-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Carmichael's emphasis on Black self-definition most directly continued the tradition of

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  1. A The NAACP's legal-integration strategy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  2. B Southern white paternalism
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  3. C Marcus Garvey's Black nationalism
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  4. D The Tuskegee model of industrial education
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Garvey's Universal Negro Improvement Association (1910s-20s) preached Black pride, economic self-sufficiency, and self-definition -- 'Black is beautiful' a generation early. Carmichael's insistence that Black people name their own struggle is Garvey's nationalism reborn. The NAACP's legalism, white paternalism, and Tuskegee's industrial training point the other way.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • A: The NAACP's legal-integration strategy was the opposite tradition — working through the courts for integration, not asserting separate Black self-definition. Carmichael was breaking with that approach, not continuing it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • B: Southern white paternalism was the enemy's tradition, not Carmichael's — whites defining what was best for Black people was exactly what he rejected.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • C: Correct. Garvey's Universal Negro Improvement Association (1910s–20s) preached Black pride, economic self-sufficiency, and self-definition — 'Black is beautiful' a generation early. Carmichael's insistence that Black people name their own struggle is Garvey's nationalism reborn.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • D: The Tuskegee model of industrial education was Booker T. Washington's accommodationist program — training for subservient labor, not self-definition. Carmichael's tradition is Garvey's, not Tuskegee's.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  SAQ5s24-ch27-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A. Briefly explain ONE movement calling for expanded rights in the 1960s. B. Briefly explain a SECOND such movement. C. Briefly explain ONE government response to these movements.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A. African Americans pressed for full equality through sit-ins, Freedom Rides, and King's campaigns, winning the Civil Rights Act (1964) and Voting Rights Act (1965). B. Women organized for equality: NOW (1966), Ms. magazine, and the ERA campaign challenged workplace and legal discrimination. C. Government responded with landmark legislation — the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, the Great Society's anti-poverty programs, and later affirmative action.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch28-mcq-03

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Which did NOT contribute to Reagan-era deficits?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A Reduced federal tax rates
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B Surging education funding
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C Higher military spending
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D Tax-code favors for the wealthy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reagan-era deficits came from slashed tax rates, soaring military budgets, and loopholes for the wealthy — not from education spending, which stagnated despite urban schools' desperate needs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Reduced federal tax rates really did contribute to Reagan-era deficits — the 1981 cuts slashed revenue. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: Correct — this is the exception. Surging education funding did not cause the deficits — education spending stagnated despite urban schools' desperate needs. The deficits came from tax cuts, military spending, and loopholes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: Higher military spending really did contribute — Reagan's arms buildup exploded the budget. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: Tax-code favors for the wealthy really did contribute — loopholes drained revenue. This is not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MCQ5s24-ch28-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reagan's critics most emphasize

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. A The effects of the 1981–83 tax cuts
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. B The U.S. response to Libya
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. C His policies' effects on the middle and lower classes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      4. D His public image and political skill
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reagan's critics grant the tax cuts tamed inflation and his image was golden — but argue the benefits flowed upward while the middle and working classes lost ground.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A: Critics did not most emphasize the tax cuts' effects in isolation — they granted the cuts tamed inflation. The core of the critique was distributional: who gained and who lost.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • B: The U.S. response to Libya (the 1986 bombing) was not the critics' main emphasis — it was a minor episode compared with the economic critique.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • C: Correct. Reagan's critics grant that the tax cuts tamed inflation and that his image was golden — but argue the benefits flowed upward while the middle and working classes lost ground.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • D: Critics did not most emphasize his public image and political skill — they conceded those. Their emphasis was on the distributional effects of his policies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      SAQ5s24-ch28-saq-01

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A. Briefly explain ONE example of the conservative direction of the nation in the 1970s and 1980s. B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that conservative direction. C. Briefly explain ONE Cold War approach taken by a 1970s or 1980s president.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        A. Nixon's 'law and order' campaign (1968) and 'Southern strategy' courted voters alienated by civil rights, urban riots, and antiwar protest. B. Reagan's election (1980) sealed the turn: tax cuts, deregulation, and attacks on 'big government' embodied a new conservative governing creed. C. Cold War approaches varied: Nixon and Kissinger pursued détente with Moscow and the opening to China, while Reagan confronted the 'evil empire' with an arms buildup.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch29-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          All of the following helped end the Cold War EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A Reagan's military buildup
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B Arms makers' desire to end the arms race
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The weakness of the Soviet economy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D Reagan and Bush's Cold War rhetoric
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Cold War ended through Reagan's pressure, Soviet economic rot, and superpower diplomacy — not because American arms makers wanted peace; they profited from the standoff.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Reagan's military buildup really did help end the Cold War — it pressured the Soviet economy and forced the arms race to a head. This was a real factor, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Correct — this is the exception. American arms makers did not want to end the arms race — they profited from it. The Cold War ended through pressure, Soviet weakness, and diplomacy, not because weapons manufacturers wanted peace.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: The weakness of the Soviet economy really did help end the Cold War — economic rot made the arms race unsustainable. This was a real factor, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Reagan and Bush's Cold War rhetoric and diplomacy really did help — pressure plus negotiation. This was a real factor, not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch29-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Clinton was a formidable opponent for Republicans for all of the following EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A His ability to win over the New Right
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B His support in the Black community
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C His talent for co-opting Republican positions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D His ability to survive scandal
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: A

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Clinton survived scandal, kept Black voters loyal, and stole GOP issues — but the New Right loathed him; winning them over was the one thing he never did.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Correct — this is the exception. Clinton never won over the New Right — it loathed him, from the 1994 Republican Revolution to impeachment. Winning them over was the one thing he never did.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Clinton's support in the Black community really did make him formidable — he kept Black voters loyal through two terms. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: Clinton's talent for co-opting Republican positions really did make him formidable — welfare reform, balanced budgets, crime bills. This is not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: Clinton's ability to survive scandal really did make him formidable — he weathered scandals that would have sunk other presidents. This is not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch29-mcq-06

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A historian using Greenspan's 1996 remarks as evidence about Federal Reserve policymaking should recognize that

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A the remarks prove the Fed had already decided to raise interest rates again and again until stock prices finally fell
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B the remarks are worthless as evidence, because public statements by central bankers never reveal what they really think
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C the remarks reveal a chairman weighing low, stable inflation against overheating markets — without committing to action
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D the remarks show Greenspan believed inflation had already returned to dangerous levels by 1996
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Greenspan's 1996 remarks show a central banker pulled in two directions — celebrating low, stable inflation while worrying aloud that markets might be overheating — without committing the Fed to any action. They are a window into the Fed's thinking, not proof of a decided policy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: Greenspan asked questions; he announced no decision. The Fed never adopted a policy of targeting asset prices, so the remarks cannot prove the Fed had decided to keep raising rates until stocks fell.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Carefully worded public remarks are still usable evidence — historians judge what a statement reveals about the speaker's concerns. Dismissing every public statement by an official as worthless would leave most policymaking history blank.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: Correct. Greenspan is visibly weighing two facts — sustained low inflation was working, yet markets might be overheating — while committing to nothing. The remarks reveal the Fed's dilemma, not a decided policy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: The passage says the opposite: Greenspan credited sustained low inflation with reducing uncertainty and risk premiums. He worried that inflation's success sat alongside possible market excess — not that inflation had already returned.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • minor · answer_tell — only one distractor uses absolute wording
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch29-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The 'irrational exuberance' Greenspan warned about ended with

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A The Great Depression
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B The stock market crash of 1987
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The dot-com crash of 2000-2001
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D The financial crisis of 2008
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The dot-com mania Greenspan named in 1996 peaked in March 2000 and then collapsed -- the NASDAQ lost nearly four-fifths of its value by 2002. The 2008 crisis was a housing bubble, 1987 a one-day crash, and the Depression a different era entirely.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: The Great Depression belonged to a different era — the 1930s, sixty years before Greenspan's 1996 warning. The 'irrational exuberance' episode was the 1990s stock mania.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: The 1987 crash was a one-day crash, not the end of the 1990s mania — Greenspan spoke in 1996, nine years after 1987, about the bubble then building.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: Correct. The dot-com mania Greenspan named in 1996 peaked in March 2000 and then collapsed — the NASDAQ lost nearly four-fifths of its value by 2002.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: The 2008 financial crisis was a housing bubble, not the stock mania Greenspan named in 1996. The 'irrational exuberance' bubble was the dot-com crash.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MCQ5s24-ch29-mcq-08

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Greenspan's public worry about asset bubbles most directly contrasts with the Federal Reserve's stance in

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. A World War II, when the Fed pegged interest rates to finance the war
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. B The late 1920s, when the Fed did little to restrain stock speculation
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. C The early 1930s, when the Fed aggressively expanded credit
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. D The 2010s, when the Fed raised interest rates rapidly
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Key: B

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In 1928-29 the Federal Reserve watched speculation mount and acted timidly and too late -- the lesson Greenspan was determined not to repeat. His 1996 warning was the 1929 failure in reverse: a central banker publicly fretting about asset prices before the crash. The 1930s Fed contracted credit, the 1940s Fed pegged rates for war finance, and the 2010s Fed moved slowly, not rapidly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A: During World War II the Fed pegged interest rates to finance the war — a policy of accommodation for war finance, not a stance on asset bubbles. It is not the contrast Greenspan's warning draws.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • B: Correct. In 1928–29 the Federal Reserve watched speculation mount and acted timidly and too late. Greenspan's 1996 public worry about asset prices was the 1929 failure in reverse — a central banker fretting about a bubble before the crash.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • C: The early-1930s Fed contracted credit, worsening the Depression — it did not aggressively expand it. And its stance was not about worrying over bubbles; the question asks for the contrast with Greenspan's bubble-worry.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • D: The 2010s Fed raised rates slowly and gradually, not rapidly — and its stance was not the 'watch speculation and do little' failure of 1929. The direct contrast is the late 1920s.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A. With the Soviet threat gone, America cut defense spending (the 'peace dividend') and shifted to humanitarian and regional interventions, as in Somalia and the Balkans. B.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               2. B Limits on abortion
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C Income-tax cuts for the wealthy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch30-mcq-04

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              All of the following hurt John Kerry in 2004 EXCEPT

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A His Vietnam-era antiwar statements
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B His voting record on the Iraq War
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C His performance in the 2004 debates
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D State ballot measures on social issues
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Kerry was wounded by his antiwar testimony, his Iraq War vote flip-flop, and ballot measures on gay marriage that turned out conservatives — but his debate performances were widely judged strong.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Kerry's Vietnam-era antiwar statements really did hurt him — the Swift Boat campaign made his 1971 testimony a liability. This was a real wound, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Kerry's voting record on the Iraq War really did hurt him — the 'I voted for it before I voted against it' flip-flop. This was a real wound, not the exception.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct — this is the exception. Kerry's debate performances in 2004 were widely judged strong — the debates were his bright spot, not his weakness.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: State ballot measures on social issues really did hurt him — gay-marriage bans turned out conservative voters in key states. This was a real wound, not the exception.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch30-mcq-05

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A historian claims George W. Bush's democracy agenda in the Middle East was a direct continuation of Wilsonian internationalism. Which of the following best evaluates the historian's claim?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A The claim is entirely correct: Bush simply continued Wilson's foreign policy, identical in both its democratic goals and its methods of achieving them in every part of the world
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B The claim fails because Wilson refused to send American troops into any foreign country, ruling out any parallel with Bush
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C The claim fails because Bush never invoked the spread of democracy to justify the invasion of Iraq
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D The claim needs qualifying: Bush borrowed Wilson's language of democracy, but Wilson worked through international institutions while Bush waged unilateral preventive war
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Bush echoed Wilson's moral language -- the Fourteen Points' call to spread democracy and the 'Freedom Agenda' -- but the comparison breaks on methods. Wilson built democracy promotion into international institutions like the League of Nations; Bush bypassed the United Nations and invaded Iraq in a preventive war. Same vocabulary, different machinery.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Bush did not continue Wilson's methods. Wilson built democracy-spreading into international institutions -- the League of Nations and collective security -- while Bush bypassed the United Nations and waged preventive war in Iraq. Identical goals and methods is an overgeneralization.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Wilson did send American troops abroad -- Veracruz in 1914, Haiti in 1915, the Dominican Republic in 1916, and Siberia in 1918. The claim cannot fail on non-interventionism because Wilson was not a non-interventionist.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Bush invoked democracy repeatedly to justify the Iraq War -- his 'Freedom Agenda' made spreading democracy the moral center of the war's public case. He never avoided that language.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Correct. The rhetoric matches -- both presidents made spreading democracy the moral center of their foreign policy -- but the methods diverge: Wilson worked through international institutions like the League of Nations, while Bush waged unilateral preventive war in Iraq without United Nations authorization.
