                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch30-mcq-06

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Giuliani delivered these remarks weeks after September 11, 2001. A historian evaluating the remarks' purpose would most accurately conclude that

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A they functioned as a legal brief that gave Congress the legal authority it needed to approve the invasion of Iraq
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B they prove Giuliani opposed any diplomacy with any foreign nation
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C they were meant to rally support for a forceful response by placing terrorism beyond any political excuse
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D they were addressed mainly to future historians studying the September 11 attacks
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Delivered weeks after September 11, Giuliani's remarks were a call for resolve at home and abroad — framing the attacks as beyond any political justification so that a forceful response would command broad support. A mayor's speech carries no legal authority, and the Iraq decision came eighteen months later.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Iraq was invaded in 2003, eighteen months after these remarks, under a separate 2002 congressional authorization — and a New York mayor's speech is not a legal brief and cannot authorize a war. The timing and the authority are both wrong.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Giuliani demanded that terrorists and their sponsors be held to account — he did not call for ending diplomacy with every foreign nation. The speech rejects excuses for terrorism, not foreign relations in general.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Correct. Giuliani is framing the attacks as beyond any political excuse — 'there was no excuse for mass murder' — precisely to unite the public and other nations behind a forceful response. The remarks are persuasion, not law.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Speakers in September 2001 addressed the living — fellow citizens and world leaders — not historians of the future. Historians use the remarks as evidence today, but that was not their purpose.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MCQ5s24-ch30-mcq-07

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In response to the September 11 attacks, Congress

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1. A declared war on Iraq immediately
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              2. B cut the American defense budget
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3. C abolished the Central Intelligence Agency
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              4. D authorized military force against those responsible for the attacks
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Key: D

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Days after September 11, Congress passed the Authorization for Use of Military Force against those responsible -- the legal foundation for the Afghanistan campaign and much that followed. The Iraq invasion came eighteen months later under a separate 2002 authorization; defense spending rose, and the CIA was expanded, not abolished.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • A: Congress did not declare war on Iraq immediately after 9/11 — the Iraq invasion came eighteen months later under a separate 2002 authorization. The immediate response was the AUMF against those responsible for the attacks.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • B: Congress did not cut the defense budget after 9/11 — defense spending rose sharply. Cuts were the opposite of what happened.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • C: Congress did not abolish the CIA — the agency was expanded and given new counterterrorism powers. Abolition was never on the table.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • D: Correct. Days after September 11, Congress passed the Authorization for Use of Military Force against those responsible — the legal foundation for the Afghanistan campaign and much that followed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      DAY-ITEM5s24-day-002

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Place the following European explorers in chronological order: Christopher Columbus, Marco Polo, Vasco Nuñez de Balboa. Why are each of these explorers important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The proper chronological order is Polo, Columbus, Balboa. Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant who traveled to China in the late 1200s. When Polo’s account of his voyage was published many years later in 1477, it spurred European desires to find a way to the rich markets of the Far East. Looking for Asia by sailing west across the Atlantic, Columbus instead discovered a New World in 1492.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          DAY-ITEM5s24-day-003

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Connect the following events with the proper decade. Events: The Spanish conquest of Mexico The Portuguese explorations of the African coast and discovery of the Cape of Good Hope The Spanish conquest of Peru The first exploration of Christopher Columbus Spanish expeditions into the American Southwest Decades: 1480–1490 1490–1500 1520–1530 1530–1540 1540–1550

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Portuguese mariners were exploring the Atlantic coastline of Africa in the 1480s. In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias discovered the Cape of Good Hope. Columbus first reached the western hemisphere in 1492. Hernando Cortès captured the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan in 1521. This broke the power of the Aztec empire and secured his conquest of Mexico.

Is his assessment fully positive or negative?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Prescott’s The History of the Conquest of Mexico combines excellent scholarship with a nineteenth-century Romantic sensibility that makes it a dramatic and colorful narrative. Prescott admires Cortès and sees him as a great Romantic hero, bending events to his will. However, as a nineteenth-century man, Prescott deplores the conquistador’s cruelty and religious fanaticism.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is Crusades, astrolabe, encomienda. The Crusades were religious wars waged by Christian Europeans in the Middle Ages. The Europeans hoped to stop Islamic territorial advances and to win back control of the Holy Land. The astrolabe was a navigational device that helped European mariners calculate their latitude.

What would he have thought of the behavior of Spanish settlers in the New World?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Bartolomé de Las Casas was a Dominican friar who opposed the mistreatment of Native Americans and in person and in print defended their humanity and rights. While Las Casas had some influence on government policy, his attitudes had little impact on most Spanish settlers. Aside from converting Native Americans to Christianity, the settlers were intent on using conquered peoples as a source of labor.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The Castillo de San Marcos is an imposing edifice that tells someone looking at it that the Spanish came to stay in America. The Castillo is the oldest surviving masonry fort in the continental United States.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The English settled Jamestown in 1607. This was the first successful English colony in America. Samuel de Champlain founded the French settlement of Quebec in 1608. The Virginia House of Burgesses, the first colonial legislature, began meeting in 1619. The Pilgrims landed at Plymouth in 1620. The Puritans established the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1629. The first settlers arrived in Maryland in 1634.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  DAY-ITEM5s24-day-009

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  How did the Spanish, French, and English differ in their treatment of Native Americans? Give examples to illustrate the differences.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    All Europeans, whatever their nationality, regarded the Native Americans as heathen barbarians. The Spanish attempted to convert the Native Americans to Christianity, and then integrate them as workers in the colonial economic and social structure. Examples would be the encomiendas of early Spanish settlers and the missions established by the Franciscans and other religious orders in the Southwest and California.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Place the following European explorers in chronological order: Robert La Salle, Henry Hudson, Jacques Cartier. Why are each of these explorers important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The proper chronological order is Cartier, Hudson, and La Salle. Jacques Cartier made three voyages to Canada in the 1530s and 1540s, exploring the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the St. Lawrence River. His voyages helped lay the foundation for New France. Henry Hudson was an English sea captain working for the Dutch East India Company. In 1609, Hudson explored Manhattan and the river that would be named after him.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          DAY-ITEM5s24-day-011

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What was the purpose of the first Thanksgiving? How has the meaning of the holiday changed over time?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The first Thanksgiving took place in November 1621, when the Pilgrims, with some Wampanoag Indian guests, celebrated a good harvest after the hardships that they had suffered in their first year in America. Thanksgiving did not become a national holiday until 1863, following a proclamation by President Abraham Lincoln.

Why is this important for American history?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Roger Williams was a Puritan minister and theologian who came to believe that church and state should be separated. His criticism of the Puritan establishment in Massachusetts led to the colony’s authorities ordering his banishment in 1635. In 1636, Williams and some followers established a new settlement at Providence in what became the colony of Rhode Island. Settlers here were assured freedom of conscience.

Why are each of these people important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is John Smith, Squanto, Anne Hutchinson. John Smith was the military man whose leadership contributed to the survival of the English colony at Jamestown, Virginia. He claimed that after being captured by Native American members of the Powhatan Confederacy, his life was saved by Pocahontas, the daughter of their chief. Squanto was a member of the Patuxet tribe.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      DAY-ITEM5s24-day-014

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Distinguish between Roman Catholicism, the Church of England, and Puritanism. How did these influence English colonization in America?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Roman Catholicism was the Christian church of Europe before the Reformation. The clergy of the Church were organized hierarchically, with the Pope at their head. Roman Catholicism emphasized regular attendance at the Mass and other liturgies, sacraments, and the performance of good works as a means to salvation. King Henry VIII created the Church of England when he broke with the Catholic Church in the 1530s.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            King William’s War began in 1688 and raged until 1697. In Europe it was known as the War of the League of Augsburg. Queen Anne’s War began in 1702 and ended in 1713. In Europe it was known as the War of the Spanish Succession. The religious revival of the Great Awakening began in the 1720s and lasted into the 1740s. The Stono Rebellion, a slave uprising in South Carolina, took place in 1739.

At one point, the play’s protagonist declares: Why did Miller see a similarity between the Salem Witch Trials and the Second Red Scare? Why does he have his protagonist condemn himself as well as his judges?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Arthur Miller saw the Salem Witch Trials and the Second Red Scare as comparable because he believed both were hysterical reactions against imaginary threats. He opposed the investigations of the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) into the political beliefs of filmmakers, writers, and actors.

Why are these events important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is the English Civil War, the Glorious Revolution, and the Acts of Union between England and Scotland. The English Civil War lasted from 1642 to 1651 and resulted in the execution of King Charles I and the establishment of a Puritan dictatorship under Oliver Cromwell.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The Byrd family’s mansion of Westover was built around 1750. It is a magnificent example of Georgian architecture. Westover testifies to the wealth of some Virginia planters. It also testifies to the high level of culture of some planters; the Byrd library was once one of the largest in America.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          DAY-ITEM5s24-day-019

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What is the difference between mercantilism and free trade? What are some examples of mercantilism in action in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries? Who was the greatest eighteenth-century British advocate of free trade?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Mercantilism was an economic theory that encouraged governments to increase their share of limited global wealth by maintaining a favorable balance of trade. This was accomplished by regulations that encouraged exports while restricting imports from foreign countries with high tariffs. Colonies provided raw materials and staple products that were turned into finished goods by the mother country. The greatest eighteenth-century British advocate of free trade was Adam Smith, whose The Wealth of Nations (1776) argued that free markets and the division of labor create national wealth.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is Nathaniel Bacon, Sir Edmund Andros, and Jonathan Edwards. Nathaniel Bacon was a Virginia planter who led a rebellion against the Royal Governor William Berkeley in 1676. Bacon was protesting the inability of Berkeley to protect settlers on the frontier from Native American attacks. After initial success, Bacon died and Berkeley reasserted control over Virginia.

What does it tell you about warfare in America during the eighteenth century?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In the eighteenth century, there were few roads in America. The easiest and fastest way to get around was by water. Lake Champlain was important because it provided an invasion route to and from Canada. Forts on the lake helped control this strategic waterway for the French, British, and later, the Americans. The French Fort Carillon was renamed Ticonderoga after it was captured by the British in 1759.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Many American colonists supported the slogan “no taxation without representation.” The British government argued that the colonists enjoyed “virtual representation.” Distinguish between these two positions. Why was the difference important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Traditionally in English history, kings had to go to parliament to raise taxes, establishing the precedent that taxpayers had to have a say on taxes that affected them. The 1689 English Bill of Rights codified the principle that all taxes had to be approved by Parliament. During the long period of Salutary Neglect, the American colonists became accustomed to paying taxes voted by their legislatures.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        During the first years of the Revolutionary War, Benedict Arnold was one of the bravest and most effective combat generals in the Continental Army.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Thomas Paine’s pamphlet Common Sense was published in January 1776 and made a powerful case for American independence from Great Britain. It was the place where George Washington was appointed the commander of the Continental Army, and the Declaration of Independence was signed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        In both 1775 at Lexington, and in 1786 during Shays’ Rebellion, Massachusetts farmers were resisting taxation that they believed was unfair.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Mercy Otis Warren was the sister of James Otis and the wife of James Warren, both prominent leaders in the resistance to British policies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       DAY-ITEM5s24-day-039

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Martha Ballard was a midwife who lived in Maine. At the age of 50, she began a diary, which she maintained for 27 years until her death. In this diary, Ballard kept a brief record of her daily activities, including visits to women in childbirth and ailing neighbors, and also the comings and goings of family members, friends, and neighbors. The historian Laurel Thatcher Ulrich used the diary to write a biography of Ballard entitled A Midwife’s Tale (1990) that was awarded the Pulitzer Prize and several other awards. Clearly a source like Martha Ballard’s diary is not as easy to read as the public papers and memoirs left by important leaders. Why are sources like this diary important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Sources like Martha Ballard’s diary, if studied carefully, can give historians valuable insights into the lives of ordinary men and women. Martha Ballard’s record of her daily activities is especially useful for shedding light on the lives of women on the American frontier in the late eighteenth century, providing important information on people whose lives were generally ignored by contemporary historians.

George Washington issued the Declaration of Neutrality in 1793.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               DAY-ITEM5s24-day-041

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Distinguish between the constitutional ideas of Thomas Jefferson and Alexander Hamilton. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Thomas Jefferson took a strict constructionist view of the Constitution. He believed that the federal government could not take any action that was not explicitly spelled out in the Constitution. Hence he opposed Alexander Hamilton’s plan for a Bank of the United States, because there is nothing in the Constitution about a national bank. Alexander Hamilton took a loose constructionist view of the Constitution.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The proper chronological order is Embargo of 1807, Non-Intercourse Act, Hartford Convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               What point is Chief Justice John Marshall making in this Supreme Court decision? Why is it important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In the Marbury v. Madison decision, Marshall made the case that since the Constitution is the supreme law of the land, the courts could void laws that conflict with the Constitution. This established the principle of judicial review, giving the courts the power to review the constitutionality of laws. This ruling enhanced the prestige and power of the judiciary.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Tecumseh was a Shawnee war leader and diplomat who in the early nineteenth century attempted to create a tribal confederacy to oppose further American settlement on Native American lands. He made it a principle that the land belonged to all Native Americans, and so no individual or group of individuals could sell parts of it to the U.S. government. Andrew Jackson was a supporter of American westward expansion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What point is Adams making in this passage of his history? What widespread view of American life does this passage reflect?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Adams is making the point that most Americans worked very hard in the early nineteenth century. They made more money than people in Europe, but had to deal with harsher living conditions. This ties into the traditional view that if you work hard in America, you can make your fortune. One of the most famous manifestations of this were the books for children written by Horatio Alger in the late nineteenth century.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Missouri Compromise was designed to keep a balance between free and slave states. In 1820, Missouri was admitted as a slave state, and Maine as a free state. The compromise, engineered by Henry Clay, drew a line through the Louisiana Territory; areas north of the line would become free states and those south of the line would become slave states.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is Bank War, Specie Circular, Panic of 1837. Henry Clay saw the Second Bank of the United States as a centerpiece of his American System. In 1832, as he prepared to run for the presidency, he attempted to have its charter renewed early by Congress. President Andrew Jackson opposed the bank as a tool of special interests. He vetoed the rechartering bill.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The Trail of Tears was the culmination of efforts by settlers to acquire the lands lived on by Native Americans in the Eastern United States. The Cherokee tribe fought back in court. In the 1831 case Cherokee Nation v. Georgia, Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the Cherokee were a “domestic dependent nation,” not a foreign state, so the Court could not hear the case; a year later, Worcester v. Georgia (1832) ruled that Georgia’s laws had no force on Cherokee land.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The proper chronological order is American Colonization Society, Nat Turner’s Rebellion, Gag Rule.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Seneca Falls Women’s Rights Convention took place on July 19–20, 1848. It was attended by such well-known activists as Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott. The African American abolitionist Frederick Douglass was also one of the attendees. The convention issued a Declaration of Sentiments that called for the right of women to vote. The convention helped spur further discussion of women’s rights.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Congressman Clement Vallandigham was a leading Northern Democratic opponent of the Civil War. Northern Democrats who opposed the war were known as Copperheads. President Abraham Lincoln took vigorous action against these Southern sympathizers. Over 14,000 were jailed without trial.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                President Abraham Lincoln proposed his Ten Percent Plan for reconstructing the Union in 1863. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is Reconstruction Act, Fifteenth Amendment, Compromise of 1877. The Reconstruction Act was passed by the Radical Republican–dominated Congress in 1867. It divided the former Confederacy into five military districts, each governed by an army general. If former Confederate states were to form new governments, they had to give freedmen equal rights and allow them to vote.

W. Griffith’s 1915 film The Birth of a Nation is an epic recounting of the Civil War and Reconstruction. This was the first great American feature film, and for many technical and artistic reasons it is a landmark in the history of cinema. Unfortunately, Griffith’s film was controversial even in 1915 for its portrayal of Reconstruction. The heroes at the end of the movie are members of the Ku Klux Klan rescuing white Southerners from freedmen and carpetbaggers. The film can be seen in whole or in part at What does this film tell us about changes in our understanding of Reconstruction? How does it illustrate changes in our understanding of race relations?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        D. W. Griffith based the latter part of The Birth of a Nation on The Clansman (1905), a racist novel by Thomas F. Dixon, Jr., which celebrated the Ku Klux Klan. The son of a former Confederate officer, Griffith was not sensitive to the appalling racism of his source material.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            President Andrew Johnson attempted to follow what he thought was Abraham Lincoln’s approach to Reconstruction. He wanted to allow the Southern states to be reorganized on lenient terms. Aside from ex-Confederate political and military leaders, and the largest plantation owners, he was willing to offer pardons to former rebels willing to swear their allegiance to the federal government.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Clara Barton’s congressional testimony reveals that there was a great deal of confusion among freedmen shortly after the Civil War. His school taught students practical skills in farming and the trades. Students built many of the early buildings at Tuskegee. The school also prepared teachers to take knowledge back to their fellow African Americans.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        A carpetbagger was a Northerner who moved to the South after the Civil War. Many were looking for economic opportunity. Others took part in the politics of Reconstruction, playing an important role in the Republican party in the Southern states. Scalawags were Southerners who cooperated with the Republican Reconstruction governments.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The federal government encouraged Western settlement. The 1862 Homestead Act granted 160 acres of land to a settler willing to farm it for five years. The Battle of the Little Bighorn took place on June 25–26, 1876. A large force of Sioux and Northern Cheyenne defeated a detachment of U.S. cavalry commanded by Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer. Custer and 267 of his men were killed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Place the following in chronological order: Sherman Antitrust Act, completion of the transcontinental railroad, Interstate Commerce Act. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The proper chronological order is completion of the transcontinental railroad, Interstate Commerce Act, Sherman Antitrust Act. The Central Pacific and Union Pacific Railroads met at Promontory Summit, Utah, on May 10, 1869. The railroads became a major driver of Western settlement and were vital to the economic interests of Western farmers.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  What does Lease reveal about the perspective of many women living on Western farms in 1891? Why is this perspective important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Mary E. Lease was a fiery spokeswoman for the Farmers’ Alliances and later the Populist Party. She expressed the concerns of Western farmers who were being squeezed by falling prices, and often found themselves unable to pay their mortgages. These farmers blamed their predicament on business monopolies and the gold standard, which contributed to a tighter money supply.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        William Jennings Bryan was a former congressman from Nebraska who captured the 1896 Democratic presidential nomination by giving a speech at the convention in which he declared, “You shall not crucify mankind upon a cross of gold!” Bryan was a spokesman for the Western farmers who believed that their economic situation was being ruined by tariffs that made prices for goods higher, and the gold standard with its tight...
