                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Place the following in chronological order: invention of barbed wire, the first “long drive” of cattle, the opening of “Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show.” Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The proper chronological order is the first “long drive” of cattle, the invention of barbed wire, and the opening of “Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show.” The first “long drive” of cattle took place in 1866, when Texas ranchers banded together and drove their herds to the railhead at Sedalia, Missouri. From there the cattle could be shipped to Chicago and Eastern markets.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Why did the U.S. government honor the Homestead Act with a national monument?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Homestead National Monument was created in 1936 on the site of the farm of Daniel Freeman at Beatrice, Nebraska. Freeman was one of the first people to take advantage of the 1862 Homestead Act, submitting his claim a few minutes after midnight on January 1, 1863. The Homestead Act played an important part in the settlement of the West as many thousands of people took advantage of its provisions to obtain land.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  DAY-ITEM5s24-day-085

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  On July 12, 1893, a young scholar named Frederick Jackson Turner gave an address to a meeting of the American Historical Association at the World Columbian Exposition in Chicago. His talk was entitled “The Significance of the Frontier in American History.” Here Turner laid the foundation for his famous “Frontier Thesis,” which argued that the frontier experience was the most important force shaping American life. He wrote, “The frontier is the line of most rapid and effective Americanization. American social development has been continually beginning over again on the frontier. This perennial rebirth, this fluidity of American life, this expansion westward with its new opportunities, its continuous touch with the simplicity of primitive society, furnish the forces dominating American character . …” Turner’s thesis made him one of the most influential historians in American history. Why did Turner’s view of Western history prove so compelling to his contemporaries?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    For all of American history up through the late nineteenth century, there had been a frontier offering Americans a chance at a new life. Following the 1890 census, the Census Bureau announced that there no longer was a continuous American frontier. This occurred just as the United States was becoming a great industrial power, with more and more Americans living in cities.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The Knights of Labor was founded in 1869. The Knights of Labor was a union that was open to all workers. The 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act prohibited the immigration of all Chinese laborers. This act was a response to anti-Chinese feeling in California and elsewhere. The Haymarket Square bombing took place on May 4, 1886, in Chicago, Illinois. As police arrived to break up a labor rally, someone threw a bomb at them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What is the perspective of AFL president Samuel Gompers in this passage? Why is this perspective important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Samuel Gompers was president of the American Federation of Labor, which was composed of unions serving skilled workers. In 1894, the American Railway Union went on strike to protest conditions at the Pullman Company, which made railroad sleeping cars. Union members refused to work on trains carrying Pullman cars. This caused chaos on the railroads. The federal government intervened against the strike.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Place the following in chronological order: Looking Backward, by Edward Bellamy; How the Other Half Lives, by Jacob Riis; Progress and Poverty, by Henry George. Why are these books important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The proper chronological order is Progress and Poverty, by Henry George; Looking Backward, by Edward Bellamy; How the Other Half Lives, by Jacob Riis. George’s Progress and Poverty (1879) attempted to explain why poverty persisted in a time of technological progress. George argued that landowners benefitted disproportionately from social progress, enabling them to charge higher rents, hurting wage-earners.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Why has the Statue of Liberty become such an important symbol?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The Statue of Liberty, or Liberty Enlightening the World, was conceived of as a gift of the French people to the United States. It was designed by Frederic Auguste Bartholdi and was constructed by Gustave Eiffel. Americans paid for the statue’s pedestal, with the money being raised by subscription. The statue was dedicated October 28, 1886.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      DAY-ITEM5s24-day-090

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      In 1873, Mark Twain and Charles Dudley Warner published a novel entitled The Gilded Age. The novel was a satire of contemporary America, condemning what the authors saw as a postwar riot of greed and public corruption. The title came from Shakespeare: “To gild refined gold, to paint the lily … is wasteful and ridiculous excess.” Twain and Warner achieved something unusual for novelists; they gave a name to a period of history. Why is the period of the late nineteenth century in the United States called the “Gilded Age”?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The late nineteenth century in the United States is called the Gilded Age because it was a time of extremes. Businessmen and industrialists made enormous fortunes while many American lived in poverty. It was a time of intense political participation by many Americans but also a time of widespread political corruption, with political machines dominating many localities.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Distinguish between vertical integration and horizontal integration. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Vertical integration and horizontal integration refer to ways in which late nineteenth-century companies structured their production. Vertical integration refers to a company controlling every phase of production from the acquisition of raw materials through manufacturing, to marketing and distribution. Horizontal integration involves a company controlling production by purchasing or merging with competitors.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Lord Bryce was a British analyst of American political institutions. What late nineteenth-century political phenomenon is he discussing here?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Lord Bryce in this passage is referring to the increasing prevalence of political machines in late nineteenth-century America. Most, though not all, political machines were located in large cities. Political machines were run by bosses, most of whom, as Bryce notes, preferred to operate behind the scenes, though some bosses held elective office.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867. Unaware of Alaska’s potential resources, many critics termed the purchase “Seward’s Folly” after Secretary of State William H. Seward. Captain Alfred Thayer Mahan’s The Influence of Sea Power upon History was published in 1890.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Place the following in chronological order: Great White Fleet, Open Door Note, Boxer Rebellion. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The proper chronological order is Open Door Note, Boxer Rebellion, Great White Fleet. Secretary of State John Hay sent his first Open Door Note to the other great powers on September 6, 1899. He proposed that the powers allow all countries to trade in China without interference. This became the foundation of the U.S. Open Door policy in China.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Distinguish between the positions of supporters and opponents of imperialism following the Spanish-American War. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            With victory in the Spanish-American War, Americans had to decide what to do about the Philippines after Commodore George Dewey won the Battle of Manila Bay. Supporters of a new American imperial role in the world believed that the United States should claim the Philippines. Theodore Roosevelt believed that the island chain offered the United States commercial advantages in the Asian market.

Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The proper chronological order is acquisition of the Panama Canal Zone, Roosevelt Corollary, Dollar Diplomacy. The United States wanted to construct a canal through the isthmus of Panama connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. In 1903, when a treaty purchasing a canal zone from Colombia fell through, President Theodore Roosevelt supported a revolution that made Panama independent.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Leonard Wood was Theodore Roosevelt’s partner in creating the 1st Volunteer Cavalry, the famous “Rough Riders.” During the Spanish-American War he was rapidly promoted, and after the conflict he became the military governor of Cuba. What is Wood’s perspective on his role as military governor? What insight does this give us into American imperial attitudes?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Leonard Wood saw the role of the U.S. Army as supporting the Cuban people as they created civil government after years of rule by Spain. As governor of Cuba, Wood not only fostered the beginnings of democratic institutions, he also launched a public health campaign that greatly reduced the dangers posed by diseases like yellow fever. Wood is seen as a sort of Progressive reformer who operated overseas.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Go to this Library of Congress page on the Panama Canal: This page features a silent film on the making of the Panama Canal that was produced in the 1920s. What perspective does the film take toward Theodore Roosevelt and his efforts to build a canal? What is the perspective of the film on the American role in building the canal?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The film takes a very positive perspective on Theodore Roosevelt’s role in building the Panama Canal. Roosevelt is seen as completing Christopher Columbus’s mission of discovery and exploration, looking for a route to the Indies. The canal is seen as a triumph of American energy, enterprise, and engineering. The film sees the canal as a measure of the U.S. position at the forefront of progress.

He was elected president in his own right in 1904, defeating the Democratic candidate Judge Alton B. Parker. The 1906 Hepburn Act gave the Interstate Commerce Commission greater regulatory authority over railroads, including the power to set maximum railroad rates.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Look up the definition of muckraker. The term received its modern meaning from President Theodore Roosevelt in a speech on April 14, 1906. While Roosevelt approved of journalistic exposures of corruption, he cautioned that too many reporters could not tear themselves away from raking muck, like a character in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (1678). Despite, Roosevelt’s criticism, the term muckraker soon became a source of pride to investigative journalists. Why were muckrakers important in the Progressive Era?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Muckrakers played an important role in publicizing corporate abuses, political malfeasance, and other social problems during the Progressive Era. They helped mobilize public opinion behind progressive reforms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Place the following in chronological order: Ballinger-Pinchot Affair, Northern Securities Case, Sixteenth Amendment. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The proper chronological order is Northern Securities Case, Ballinger-Pinchot Affair, and Sixteenth Amendment. The Northern Securities Company was organized in 1901 by James J. Hill, E. H. Harriman, and J. P. Morgan, and controlled a number of railroads. In 1902, President Theodore Roosevelt directed the Justice Department to sue for the dissolution of the company under the Sherman Antitrust Act.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              This passage is a newspaper account of the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire. Because of poor safety conditions, including doors to stairwells that had been chained shut to prevent possible thefts, 146 workers, mostly young women, died when fire swept through the Triangle Shirtwaist Company on the eighth, ninth, and tenth floors of the Asch Building in New York City. What were some of the consequences of this tragedy?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The disastrous Triangle Shirtwaist Fire shocked the nation in 1911. It had immediate consequences in New York. After an investigation, new workplace safety laws were enacted in New York. The New York legislature also passed a bill to shorten workers’ hours. These bills became models for other states. The tragedy also proved a spur to unionization.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Distinguish between Theodore Roosevelt’s New Nationalism and Woodrow Wilson’s New Freedom. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Theodore Roosevelt began promulgating his New Nationalism in 1910, and it became the basis of his run for the presidency in 1912 as the candidate of the Progressive (Bull Moose) party. Roosevelt called for an expanded role for the federal government in regulating business and the economy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Zimmermann Telegram Outbreak of War in Europe Treaty of Versailles Announcement of the Fourteen Points Sussex Pledge Years: 1914 1916 1917 1918 1919

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        World War I broke out in August 1914, following a diplomatic crisis precipitated by the assassination of the Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand. The 1916 Sussex Pledge was a reaction of the Imperial German government to American criticism of its campaign of unrestricted submarine warfare against the British and French. The Germans had recently sunk the Sussex, with the loss of 50 lives.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          DAY-ITEM5s24-day-110

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          When he asked Congress to declare war on Imperial Germany, what did Woodrow Wilson believe the United States should be fighting for? Why is this important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            President Woodrow Wilson’s War Message to Congress envisioned a very idealistic war. The United States went to war because of the German submarine campaign and questions of the freedom of the seas. Wilson was interested in ensuring the freedom of the seas, but he also wanted to see a new, more democratic world emerge from the conflict. He embodied his ideas on a just peace in his Fourteen Points.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Place the following in chronological order: Lusitania, Meuse-Argonne Offensive, Lever Food and Fuel Control Act. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The proper chronological order is Lusitania, Lever Food and Fuel Control Act, Meuse-Argonne Offensive. The Lusitania was a British passenger liner that was sunk by a German submarine off the coast of Ireland on May 7, 1915. 1,198 passengers and crew lost their lives, including 128 Americans. This sinking outraged American public opinion and led to a diplomatic crisis with Germany.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  What was the purpose of Congress in passing the Sedition Act? What does this tell us about the United States during World War I?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The 1918 Sedition Act was an expansion of the 1917 Espionage Act. It was designed to quell dissent and actions that might interfere with the war effort. It was also intended to end vigilante actions by citizens against supposed traitors by giving the government the power to prosecute them. The law reflected the widespread intolerance for dissenting viewpoints on the war.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Distinguish between the supporters of the League of Nations and “reservationists.” Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        President Woodrow Wilson and supporters of the League of Nations believed that the international organization would prevent any more conflicts like World War I. Operating under the principle of collective security, member states would act to resolve international disputes and oppose unprovoked aggressions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Washington Disarmament Conference Start of Prohibition Lindbergh Flight across the Atlantic Stock Market Crash Scopes Trial Years: 1920 1921 1925 1927 1929

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A constitutional amendment to introduce national prohibition was passed by Congress in 1917 and was ratified by the states in 1919. The Volstead Act to enforce prohibition passed Congress on October 28, 1919. Prohibition went into effect on January 17, 1920. The Washington Disarmament Conference convened on November 12, 1921.
