                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The writer F. Scott Fitzgerald entitled a 1922 collection of short stories Tales of the Jazz Age. This helped popularize a term that became associated with the 1920s. Why is the “Jazz Age” an appropriate name for the decade that followed the conclusion of World War I?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The name “Jazz Age” is appropriate for the 1920s in part because this was a time when jazz music became very popular. Both African American musicians like Louis Armstrong and white jazz musicians such as the bandleader Paul Whiteman enjoyed a great deal of success. Serious composers like George Gershwin wrote music heavily influenced by jazz.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Place the following in chronological order: execution of Sacco and Vanzetti, National Origins Act, Palmer Raids. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proper chronological order is Palmer Raids, National Origins Act, execution of Sacco and Vanzetti. Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer launched the Palmer Raids between November 1919 and January 1920. These were a response to terrorist bombings. The raids rounded up thousands of left-wing radicals, and 500 were deported. This was a major moment in the first Red Scare.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      What is President Coolidge’s point in this speech? What does this say about the governing philosophy of the Republican presidential administrations of the 1920s?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        In this speech, Coolidge is making the point that decreases in government spending benefit ordinary Americans by reducing taxes, which allows them to keep more of their money. Like his predecessor Warren G. Harding, Coolidge believed in limited government. Both Harding and Coolidge cut government spending and lowered taxes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Why did Lindbergh become an international hero? What was the significance of his achievement?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            In May 1927, Charles Lindbergh became the first person to make a solo flight across the Atlantic in his plane The Spirit of St. Louis. Lindbergh was honored for his courage and skill in singlehandedly accomplishing a feat that had cost other pilots their lives. Lindbergh increased the esteem of his contemporaries through his modesty and unwillingness to financially capitalize on his achievement.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Distinguish between the views of Herbert Hoover and Alfred “Al” Smith concerning Prohibition in the 1928 presidential election. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Governor Alfred “Al” Smith of New York was the Democratic nominee for president in 1928. A native of New York City, and in his early career associated with the Tammany Hall political machine, Smith vehemently opposed Prohibition. Herbert Hoover, the Republican nominee, expressed some support for Prohibition, calling it an “experiment noble in purpose.” Hoover, famous as a philanthropist and energetic public servant,...

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  What social development is Frederick Lewis Allen describing in an early popular history of the 1920s? Why was this important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Frederick Lewis Allen is describing changes in the behavior of young women in the 1920s. Women had received the vote in 1920, but one of the most conspicuous developments of the decade was the growing social freedom of women. Women shed their corsets and long, heavy dresses and embraced makeup. The “flapper,” with her bobbed hair, short dress, and mannish figure became the symbol of the age.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: End of Prohibition Hawley-Smoot Tariff Scottsboro Boys Trial Reconstruction Finance Corporation Formation of the Congress of Industrial Organization (CIO) Years: 1930 1931 1932 1933 1935

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The 1930 Hawley-Smoot Tariff was intended to protect American industries and jobs by making foreign goods more expensive. It had the unintended effect of leading other countries to increase their tariffs, hurting foreign trade and Americans who worked in industries that exported goods. The 1931 Scottsboro Boys Trial involved nine African American teenagers who were convicted of raping two white women on a train.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Place the following in chronological order: Social Security Act, Justice Reorganization Bill, National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA). Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The proper chronological order is National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA), Social Security Act, Justice Reorganization Bill. The 1933 NIRA was a centerpiece of the First New Deal. The NIRA attempted to restore industrial prosperity by encouraging industries to set standards for prices and competition, while also protecting the rights of workers.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Mrs. Henderson lived in Oklahoma. What phenomenon is she describing? Why was it important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Mrs. Henderson’s letter is referring to the effects of the Dust Bowl. Beginning in 1934, a series of droughts in the 1930s dried out soil that had been exposed by years of farming in the Lower Plains states and produced immense clouds of dust. Many people lost their farms. By 1940, 3.5 million people moved away from the affected area.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Distinguish between the approaches of Herbert Hoover and Franklin D. Roosevelt in combating the Great Depression. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    It is not true that President Herbert Hoover did nothing to help people during the Great Depression. He actively used the power of the federal government to combat the depression. He cut taxes and launched public works to provide employment. He signed legislation such as the Hawley-Smoot Tariff and helped create the Reconstruction Finance Corporation (RFC) to pump money into the economy by lending money to banks and...

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Why was Franklin D. Roosevelt so effective as a leader?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Although Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal failed to end the Great Depression, he did build a New Deal Coalition that endured for many decades. Born to wealth, as his home indicates, FDR had a capacity to empathize and communicate with ordinary Americans. Some scholars attribute this to his long struggle with the polio that crippled his legs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Robert Penn Warren’s great novel All the King’s Men was about a southern politician loosely based on Louisiana’s Huey P. Long. In the passage above, the novel’s narrator Jack Burden reflects on Willie Stark, his former boss. Why would a figure like Huey P. Long evoke such mixed emotions?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Huey P. Long served as governor of Louisiana from 1928–1932, and as U.S. senator from 1932–1935. Long built a political machine in Louisiana that made him the virtual dictator of the state. He remained very popular in Louisiana because he spoke up for the poor, built a string of charity hospitals, and expanded schools, with free textbooks for schoolchildren. As an ambitious senator, Long aimed for the presidency.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Distinguish between the First and Second New Deals. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    President Franklin D. Roosevelt promoted recovery, relief, and reform in his New Deal Program. The First New Deal of 1933–1934 emphasized recovery and relief, with agencies such as the National Recovery Administration (NRA), Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), and the Agricultural Adjustment Administration (AAA).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: First Neutrality Act German Invasion of Poland Lend-Lease Act Destroyers for Bases Agreement Internment Camps for Japanese established Years: 1935 1939 1940 1941 1942

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The Neutrality Act of 1935 was an effort to keep the United States out of a conflict like World War I. The law established a six-month moratorium on American trade in weapons or military supplies with warring countries. Following the signing of a nonaggression pact with the Soviet Union, Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, beginning World War II.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Place the following in chronological order: Battle of the Bulge, Battle of Midway, Battle of Guadalcanal. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The proper chronological order is Battle of Midway, Battle of Guadalcanal, and Battle of the Bulge. The Battle of Midway, fought June 4–7, 1942, turned the tide of the war in the Pacific Theater. In a battle dominated by aircraft carriers, the Americans sank four Japanese aircraft carriers while losing one aircraft carrier of their own. After this defeat, the Japanese were forced on the defensive.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              DAY-ITEM5s24-day-132

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              What foreign policy position is Senator Nye taking in the passage above? How influential was this perspective?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Senator Gerald P. Nye of North Dakota was an influential isolationist. From 1934 to 1936, Nye headed a Senate investigation into the munitions industry to see if prominent American businesses had helped lead the United States into World War I. He played an important role in passing the neutrality laws designed to keep the United States out of another war. Nye opposed American intervention in World War II.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  DAY-ITEM5s24-day-133

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Why is what happened on December 7, 1941, so important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The World War II Valor in the Pacific National Monument lies above the resting place of the USS Arizona. During the December 7, 1941, Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, the Arizona, an American battleship, was sunk with the loss of 1,177 men. In all, during the Japanese assault, 2,403 Americans were killed and 1,178 were wounded. The United States and Japan disagreed over Japanese conquests in China and Indochina.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      DAY-ITEM5s24-day-134

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Place the following in chronological order: Beginning of the draft, G.I. Bill, Revenue Act of 1942. Why are these important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The proper chronological order is beginning of the draft, Revenue Act of 1942, G.I. Bill. In 1940, in response to the security threat posed by the outbreak of World War II and Axis victories, the United States launched a massive rearmament program to build up American defenses. Part of this program was the institution of a draft to build up the army.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Distinguish between the narrow front and broad front strategies in the European Theater of World War II. Why is this distinction important?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Following the Allied breakout from the D-Day beachhead in July, 1944, a dispute arose over the best way to complete the rout of the German armies and end the war. The Allied armies moved so fast that they began to outrun available supplies, especially gasoline. The British General Bernard Montgomery argued for a narrow front thrust into Germany by his forces.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              DAY-ITEM5s24-day-136

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Paul Fussell was a distinguished professor of literature and writer, who in his youth had served as an infantry officer in the European Theater of World War II. His essay “Thank God for the Atomic Bomb” was a response to critics who argued that the dropping of the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki was immoral. What is his perspective, and why is it significant?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                By August 1945, Japan was isolated and objectively beaten. Despite this, the military rulers of Japan declared that they would fight on and were gathering large forces to resist an American invasion. The Americans were preparing Operation Olympic, an assault on the Japanese home islands.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  QA findings

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • No findings
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  DAY-ITEM5s24-day-137

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Federal Employee Loyalty Program Winston Churchill’s “Iron Curtain” Speech Start of the Korean War Yalta Conference Establishment of the Communist People’s Republic of China Years: 1945 1946 1947 1949 1950

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The February 1945 Yalta Conference between President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Josef Stalin discussed postwar conditions in Europe. Stalin promised free elections in Poland, a pledge he later broke. On March 5, 1946, Winston Churchill, now out of office, gave his “Iron Curtain” speech while visiting the United States.
