                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Assess how far the abolitionist movement fostered change in America between 1830 and 1860.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    {'thesis': 'The abolitionist movement forced slavery onto the national agenda and reshaped politics, building mass antislavery sentiment and new political organizations - though it freed few enslaved people directly before the Civil War.', 'evidence': ["William Lloyd Garrison's Liberator (1831) and the American Anti-Slavery Society spread immediatist abolitionism through print and petition campaigns", "The Underground Railroad and slave narratives (e.g., Frederick Douglass) made slavery's horrors concrete for northern audiences", 'Political impact: abolitionism fed the Liberty Party, Free Soil Party, and the Republican Party, while the gag rule and mob violence showed fierce resistance']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        {'thesis': "Social movements fundamentally reshaped postwar American society: the civil rights movement dismantled legal segregation, the women's movement expanded economic and political equality, and the counterculture challenged traditional norms - though each faced backlash that limited change.", 'evidence': ['Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965 ended Jim Crow and enfranchised Black southerners', "Title IX (1972) and Roe v. Wade (1973) advanced women's equality in education and reproductive rights", "Conservative backlash - Nixon's 'silent majority,' the Reagan coalition of 1980 - showed the limits and reversals of movement gains"]}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Assess how far the relationship between the American colonists and Great Britain changed from 1750 to 1783.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            {'thesis': "The colonists' relationship with Britain changed profoundly from loyal subjects under salutary neglect to independent citizens of a new republic, as imperial reforms after 1763 provoked resistance that escalated from protest to revolution - though a substantial Loyalist minority never accepted the break.", 'evidence': ['Stamp Act (1765) and Intolerable Acts (1774) ended salutary neglect and unified colonial resistance', 'Shift from the Olive Branch Petition (1775) seeking reconciliation to the Declaration of Independence (1776)', 'Continuity: roughly one-fifth of colonists remained Loyalists, and many Patriots still admired British constitutional ideals']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                {'thesis': "The postwar federal government was deeply compromised by corruption: rapid economic expansion, weak regulation, and machine politics produced systemic graft, though reform movements began to check it by century's end.", 'evidence': ['Grant-era scandals - the Credit Mobilier scheme and the Whiskey Ring - implicated congressmen and cabinet officials', "Urban machines such as Tweed's Tammany Hall traded contracts and jobs for votes and kickbacks", 'Reform responses: the Pendleton Civil Service Act (1883) and the Interstate Commerce Act (1887) began curbing the spoils system and railroad abuses']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Assess how far the temperance and Prohibition movements transformed American society between 1890 and 1935.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    {'thesis': "Temperance and Prohibition briefly transformed American law and daily life - achieving a constitutional ban on alcohol - but the experiment's failures, from organized crime to mass noncompliance, showed the limits of legislating morality, ending in repeal.", 'evidence': ['The WCTU and Anti-Saloon League built a mass moral-reform movement that won the 18th Amendment (1919)', "Prohibition fueled speakeasies, bootlegging, and organized crime (e.g., Capone's Chicago empire), undermining respect for law", 'The 21st Amendment (1933) repealed Prohibition, marking the only constitutional amendment ever reversed']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Assess how far the Massachusetts Bay Colony differed from the Virginia colony between 1607 and 1754.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        {'thesis': 'Massachusetts Bay and Virginia differed fundamentally in purpose and social order - a Puritan religious refuge built on towns and families versus a profit-driven plantation colony built on bound labor - though both shared an English identity and displaced Native peoples.', 'evidence': ["Massachusetts Bay: Puritan mission ('city upon a hill'), town meetings, family farms; Virginia: joint-stock venture, House of Burgesses, tobacco plantations", 'Labor systems diverged: New England relied on family and town labor while Virginia moved from indentured servitude to enslaved labor', "Similarity: both maintained English legal traditions and a strong English identity, and both expanded at Native Americans' expense"]}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            {'thesis': "Women's public roles expanded dramatically after 1920 through suffrage, wartime work, and new social freedoms, yet the postwar domestic ideal and continued exclusion from political power show how much continuity persisted.", 'evidence': ['The 19th Amendment (1920) enfranchised women; flappers and new employment challenged Victorian norms', "World War II drew millions of women into factories and services ('Rosie the Riveter')", 'Continuity: the 1950s suburban domestic ideal, few women in Congress, and persistent wage gaps limited change']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Assess how far industrialization affected rural and urban workers between 1865 and 1900.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                {'thesis': 'Industrialization transformed both urban and rural workers, but in different ways: city workers faced factory discipline and dangerous conditions alongside higher wages and new labor organizations, while rural workers faced mechanization and falling prices that drove the Populist revolt.', 'evidence': ["Urban: factory work brought long hours and hazards (e.g., Triangle Shirtwaist fire, 1911, rooted in this era's conditions) but also wages that drew immigrants; workers organized the Knights of Labor and the AFL", "Rural: mechanization and railroad freight rates squeezed farmers as crop prices fell, fueling the Grange and the People's (Populist) Party", 'Comparison: both groups confronted concentrated corporate power, but urban workers sought workplace protections while farmers sought economic regulation']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Assess how far the First Great Awakening transformed American national identity between 1700 and 1765.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    {'thesis': 'The First Great Awakening fostered a shared intercolonial religious experience and challenged established authority, planting seeds of a common American identity - though its effects were uneven and did not yet produce political unity.', 'evidence': ['Itinerant preachers like George Whitefield and Gilbert Tennent drew massive intercolonial crowds and challenged Anglican and Congregational establishments', 'The revivals encouraged individual religious judgment, weakening deference to traditional authority', 'Limits: the Awakening divided churches (Old Lights vs. New Lights) and remained a religious, not political, movement']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Assess how far social and economic issues shaped United States foreign policy between 1919 and 1933.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        {'thesis': 'Domestic social and economic pressures powerfully shaped interwar foreign policy: war debts and reparations entangled diplomacy, nativism drove immigration restriction, and the Depression deepened isolationism.', 'evidence': ['War debts and German reparations dominated 1920s diplomacy (Dawes Plan, 1924) as Americans demanded repayment', 'Nativism produced the Emergency Quota Act (1921) and the National Origins Act (1924), closing the era of open immigration', 'The Great Depression reinforced isolationism - tariff walls (Hawley-Smoot, 1930) and the Neutrality Acts reflected a turn inward']}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Convinced that the Revolution was the work of a few miscreants who had rallied an armed rabble to their cause, British leaders expected the revolutionaries to be intimidated. They believed the vast majority of Americans were loyal but cowed by Patriot terror tactics, and would rise up, drive out the rebels, and restore loyal government in each colony.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A. Briefly explain one point of view about the American Revolution that the author describes in the passage. B. Briefly explain one piece of evidence from 1763 to 1800, not mentioned in the passage, that supports the point of view described. C. Briefly explain one piece of evidence from 1763 to 1800, not mentioned in the passage, that refutes the point of view described.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ['The author describes the British point of view: that most colonists were loyal to the Crown and that the Revolution was the work of a small radical minority terrorizing the majority into silence.', 'The Olive Branch Petition of 1775 supports this view - even after fighting began at Lexington and Concord, the Continental Congress still petitioned George III for reconciliation, showing reluctance to break with Britain.', "Thomas Paine's Common Sense (1776) refutes it - the pamphlet's enormous popular readership showed broad popular enthusiasm for independence, not a cowed loyal majority."]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Society in every state is a blessing, but government even in its best state is but a necessary evil; in its worst state an intolerable one; for when we suffer, or are exposed to the same miseries by a government, which we might expect in a country without government, our calamity is heightened by reflecting that we furnish the means by which we suffer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A. Briefly explain Paine's purpose in writing Common Sense. B. Briefly explain how the argument in the excerpt reflects one debate among colonists between 1763 and 1776. C. Briefly explain one effect of publications like Common Sense on the movement for independence.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ['Paine aimed to persuade ordinary colonists that monarchy was illegitimate and that independence was both necessary and achievable.', "The attack on government as a 'necessary evil' reflects the colonial debate over whether Parliament had any legitimate authority over the colonies after the Stamp Act and Townshend duties.", 'Common Sense built mass popular support for independence, helping push the Continental Congress toward the Declaration of Independence in July 1776.']

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ['The cartoon urges the colonies to unite, warning that divided they will die - the severed snake symbolizes colonies that are helpless apart.', 'Published during the French and Indian War, it called for intercolonial cooperation against the French threat, which led to the Albany Plan of Union.', "By 1776 the colonies had moved from Franklin's failed 1754 appeal to actual coordinated resistance, forming the Continental Congress and a Continental Army."]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      SAQsaq-drill-q1
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      During Reconstruction, formerly enslaved Black men voted in large numbers and held office at every level of Southern government, from local sheriffs and state legislators to members of Congress - a transformation made possible by the Reconstruction Acts and the Fifteenth Amendment. Historian Eric Foner has called Reconstruction 'America's unfinished revolution,' arguing that it was the first great experiment in interracial democracy, even though its gains were later overturned.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A. Briefly explain Foner's view of the significance of Reconstruction for Black Americans. B. Briefly explain one specific federal action between 1865 and 1877 that supports the developments Foner describes. C. Briefly explain one development after 1877 that challenged the gains Foner describes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        ["Foner views Reconstruction as America's 'unfinished revolution' - the first experiment in interracial democracy, in which Black men voted and held office across the South.", 'The Fifteenth Amendment (1870) prohibited denying the vote on account of race, giving constitutional protection to Black suffrage.', 'Southern states imposed poll taxes, literacy tests, and grandfather clauses that disenfranchised Black voters, while the Supreme Court weakened federal protection in decisions such as the Civil Rights Cases (1883).']

Source 2: 'How different would be the sensation of a philosophic mind to reflect that instead of exterminating a part of the human race by our modes of population that we had persevered through all difficulties and at last had imparted our Knowledge of cultivating and the arts, to the Aboriginals of the Country by which the source of future life and happiness had been preserved and extended.'

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ["Rowlandson portrays Native Americans as savage 'hell-hounds' who slaughtered Christians, while Knox treats them as fellow members of the human race who could be 'civilized' through American knowledge of farming and the arts.", "Rowlandson wrote as a captive during King Philip's War (1675-1676), when Wampanoag attacks had killed colonists and taken her prisoner; her terror shaped her demonizing language.", "The view of Native peoples as either savage obstacles or candidates for 'civilization' underpinned removal and assimilation policies, from the Indian Removal Act of 1830 to the reservation and boarding-school systems."]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Constitutionalism describes a complex idea, rooted in historical experience, that subjects the officials who exercise governmental powers to the limitations of a higher law. It proclaims the desirability of the rule of law as opposed to rule by the arbitrary judgment or mere fiat of public officials. The central element of constitutionalism is that government officials are not free to do anything they please in any manner they choose; they are bound to observe both the limitations on power and the procedures set out in the supreme, constitutional law of the community. The touchstone of constitutionalism is limited government under a higher law.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A. Briefly explain one claim the author makes about the nature of constitutionalism. B. Briefly explain one piece of evidence from the period 1787 to 1800 that supports the author's view that government power should be limited by a higher law. C. Briefly explain one development from the period 1787 to 1800 that challenged the ideal of limited government described by the author.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Answer and explanation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Key: —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ['The author claims that constitutionalism means government officials are bound by a higher law and may not exercise power arbitrarily; the test of constitutionalism is limited government under that higher law.', 'The Bill of Rights (1789-1791) supports the claim because it placed explicit written limits on federal power in order to protect individual liberties.', 'The Sedition Act of 1798 challenged the ideal because it criminalized criticism of the federal government, punishing the political speech the First Amendment was meant to protect.']
